543	@contextlib.contextmanager
544	def start_span(
545	    name: str = "span",
546	    span_type: str | None = SpanType.UNKNOWN,
547	    attributes: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
548	    trace_destination: TraceLocationBase | None = None,
549	    log_level: SpanLogLevel | str | None = None,
550	    run_id: str | None = None,
551	    links: list[Link] | None = None,
552	    description: str | None = None,
553	) -> Generator[LiveSpan, None, None]:
554	    """
555	    Context manager to create a new span and start it as the current span in the context.
556	
557	    This context manager automatically manages the span lifecycle and parent-child relationships.
558	    The span will be ended when the context manager exits. Any exception raised within the
559	    context manager will set the span status to ``ERROR``, and detailed information such as
560	    exception message and stacktrace will be recorded to the ``attributes`` field of the span.
561	    New spans can be created within the context manager, then they will be assigned as child
562	    spans.
563	
564	    .. code-block:: python
565	        :test:
566	
567	        import mlflow
568	
569	        with mlflow.start_span("my_span") as span:
570	            x = 1
571	            y = 2
572	            span.set_inputs({"x": x, "y": y})
573	
574	            z = x + y
575	
576	            span.set_outputs(z)
577	            span.set_attribute("key", "value")
578	            # do something
579	
580	    When this context manager is used in the top-level scope, i.e. not within another span context,
581	    the span will be treated as a root span. The root span doesn't have a parent reference and
582	    **the entire trace will be logged when the root span is ended**.
583	
584	
585	    .. tip::
586	
587	        If you want more explicit control over the trace lifecycle, you can use
588	        the `mlflow.start_span_no_context()` API. It provides lower
589	        level to start spans and control the parent-child relationships explicitly.
590	        However, it is generally recommended to use this context manager as long as it satisfies
591	        your requirements, because it requires less boilerplate code and is less error-prone.
592	
593	    .. note::
594	
595	        The context manager doesn't propagate the span context across threads by default. see
596	        `Multi Threading <https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracing/api/manual-instrumentation#multi-threading>`_
597	        for how to propagate the span context across threads.
598	
599	    Args:
600	        name: The name of the span.
601	        span_type: The type of the span. Can be either a string or
602	            a :py:class:`SpanType <mlflow.entities.SpanType>` enum value
603	        attributes: A dictionary of attributes to set on the span.
604	        trace_destination: The destination to log the trace to, such as MLflow Experiment. If
605	            not provided, the destination will be an active MLflow experiment or an destination
606	            set by the :py:func:`mlflow.tracing.set_destination` function. This parameter
607	            should only be used for root span and setting this for non-root spans will be
608	            ignored with a warning.
609	        log_level: Optional severity level to attach to the span. Accepts a
610	            :py:class:`SpanLogLevel <mlflow.entities.SpanLogLevel>` or its name
611	            (e.g. ``"INFO"``, ``"DEBUG"``). If not provided, the span level is
612	            resolved from the span type at end time.
613	        run_id: The ID of the MLflow run to associate with the trace. This parameter is
614	            only applied when creating a root span. If provided without an explicit
615	            `trace_destination`, the trace will be logged to the run's experiment. If an
616	            active MLflow run is already set via `mlflow.start_run()`, this parameter takes
617	            precedence over the active run.
618	        links: A list of :py:class:`Link <mlflow.entities.Link>` objects to associate with
619	            the span.
620	        description: An optional human-readable description of the span.
621	
622	    Returns:
623	        Yields an :py:class:`mlflow.entities.Span` that represents the created span.
624	    """
625	    # If tracing is disabled via context(enabled=False), return NoOpSpan
626	    config = _USER_TRACE_CONTEXT.get()
627	    if config is not None and config.enabled is False:
628	        yield NoOpSpan()
629	        return
630	
631	    try:
632	        experiment_id = getattr(trace_destination, "experiment_id", None)
633	
634	        otel_span = provider.start_span_in_context(
635	            name,
636	            experiment_id=experiment_id,
637	        )
638	
639	        # If the span was dropped by the sampler (e.g., due to sampling ratio),
640	        # still propagate the OTel context so that child spans inherit the same
641	        # trace ID and are also consistently dropped.
642	        if not otel_span.is_recording():
643	            noop_span = NoOpSpan(otel_span=otel_span)
644	        else:
645	            noop_span = None
646	
647	            # Create a new MLflow span and register it to the in-memory trace manager

1245	def search_sessions(
1246	    max_results: int = 100,
1247	    run_id: str | None = None,
1248	    model_id: str | None = None,
1249	    include_spans: bool = True,
1250	    locations: list[str] | None = None,
1251	) -> list[Session]:
1252	    """
1253	    Return complete sessions that match the given search criteria.
1254	
1255	    A session is a collection of traces that share the same session ID, typically representing
1256	    a multi-turn conversation or a series of related interactions. This API retrieves complete
1257	    sessions by first identifying unique session IDs from traces, then fetching all traces
1258	    belonging to each session in parallel.
1259	
1260	    Args:
1261	        max_results: Maximum number of sessions to return. Default is 100.
1262	        run_id: A run id to scope the search. When a trace is created under an active run,
1263	            it will be associated with the run and you can filter on the run id to retrieve
1264	            traces.
1265	        model_id: If specified, search traces associated with the given model ID.
1266	        include_spans: If ``True``, include spans in the returned traces. Otherwise, only
1267	            the trace metadata is returned. Default is ``True``.
1268	        locations: A list of locations to search over. To search over experiments, provide
1269	            a list of experiment IDs. To search over UC tables on databricks, provide
1270	            a list of locations in the format
1271	            `<catalog_name>.<schema_name>[.<table_prefix>]`.
1272	            If not provided, the search will be performed across the current active experiment.
1273	
1274	    Returns:
1275	        A list of :py:class:`Session <mlflow.entities.Session>` objects, where each session
1276	        contains :py:class:`Trace <mlflow.entities.Trace>` objects that share the same
1277	        session ID. Sessions are ordered by the timestamp of their first trace (most recent first).
1278	        Each Session object provides convenient access via ``session.id`` and supports
1279	        iteration with ``for trace in session``.
1280	
1281	    .. code-block:: python
1282	        :caption: Basic usage - search sessions in an experiment
1283	
1284	        import mlflow
1285	
1286	        # Get all sessions from the current experiment
1287	        sessions = mlflow.search_sessions()
1288	
1289	        # Each session provides convenient access to ID and traces
1290	        for session in sessions:
1291	            print(f"Session {session.id} has {len(session)} traces")
1292	            for trace in session:
1293	                print(f"  Trace: {trace.info.trace_id}")
1294	
1295	    .. code-block:: python
1296	        :caption: Use sessions with evaluation
1297	
1298	        import mlflow
1299	
1300	        # Get sessions for evaluation
1301	        sessions = mlflow.search_sessions(
1302	            locations=["experiment_id"],
1303	            max_results=50,
1304	        )
1305	
1306	        # Flatten sessions for evaluation if needed
1307	        all_traces = [trace for session in sessions for trace in session]
1308	        mlflow.genai.evaluate(data=all_traces)
1309	    """
1310	    _validate_list_param("locations", locations, allow_none=True)
1311	
1312	    if not locations:
1313	        _logger.debug("Searching sessions in the current active experiment")
1314	    locations = _get_search_locations(locations)
1315	
1316	    session_id_key = TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION
1317	
1318	    # Step 1: Page through traces to collect unique session IDs (up to max_results)
1319	    seen_session_ids: set[str] = set()
1320	    session_ids: list[str] = []
1321	    page_token: str | None = None
1322	
1323	    while len(session_ids) < max_results:
1324	        traces: list[Trace] = TracingClient().search_traces(
1325	            max_results=SEARCH_TRACES_DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS,
1326	            order_by=["timestamp DESC"],
1327	            page_token=page_token,
1328	            include_spans=False,
1329	            run_id=run_id,
1330	            model_id=model_id,
1331	            locations=locations,
1332	        )
1333	
1334	        for trace in traces:
1335	            session_id = trace.info.request_metadata.get(session_id_key)
1336	            if session_id and session_id not in seen_session_ids:
1337	                seen_session_ids.add(session_id)
1338	                session_ids.append(session_id)
1339	                if len(session_ids) >= max_results:
1340	                    break
1341	
1342	        page_token = traces.token if hasattr(traces, "token") else None
1343	        if not page_token:
1344	            break
1345	
1346	    if not session_ids:
1347	        return []
1348	
1349	    # Step 2: Fetch complete traces for each session in parallel
1350	    def fetch_session_traces(session_id: str) -> list[Trace]:
1351	        session_filter = f"metadata.`{session_id_key}` = '{session_id}'"
1352	
1353	        return search_traces(
1354	            filter_string=session_filter,
1355	            max_results=None,  # Get all traces in the session
1356	            order_by=["timestamp ASC"],  # Order by time within session
1357	            include_spans=include_spans,
1358	            run_id=run_id,
1359	            return_type="list",
1360	            model_id=model_id,
1361	            locations=locations,
1362	        )
1363	
1364	    max_workers = min(len(session_ids), MLFLOW_SEARCH_TRACES_MAX_THREADS.get())
1365	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(
1366	        max_workers=max_workers,
1367	        thread_name_prefix="search_sessions",
1368	    ) as executor:
1369	        session_results = list(map_with_context(executor, fetch_session_traces, session_ids))
1370	
1371	    # Filter out empty sessions, wrap in Session objects, and preserve order
1372	    sessions: list[Session] = [Session(s) for s in session_results if s]
1373	
1374	    return sessions

1506	def update_current_trace(
1507	    tags: dict[str, str] | None = None,
1508	    metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None,
1509	    client_request_id: str | None = None,
1510	    request_preview: str | None = None,
1511	    response_preview: str | None = None,
1512	    state: TraceState | str | None = None,

1520	    Args:

1525	            git hash of the application version that produced the trace.

1527	            useful for linking the trace back to a specific request in your application or
1528	            external system. If None, the client request ID is not updated.

1530	            By default, MLflow will truncate the trace request naively by limiting the length.
1531	            This parameter allows you to specify a custom preview string.
1532	        response_preview: A preview of the response to be shown in the Trace list view in the UI.
1533	            By default, MLflow will truncate the trace response naively by limiting the length.
1534	            This parameter allows you to specify a custom preview string.

1536	            Only "OK" and "ERROR" are allowed. This overrides the overall trace state without
1537	            affecting the status of the current span.

1539	            model ID is associated with the trace.

1541	            ``mlflow.trace.session`` key.

1543	            ``mlflow.trace.user`` key.

1545	    Example:
1546	
1547	        You can use this function either within a function decorated with ``@mlflow.trace`` or
1548	        within the scope of the `with mlflow.start_span` context manager. If there is no active
1549	        trace found, this function will raise an exception.
1550	
1551	        Using within a function decorated with `@mlflow.trace`:
1552	
1553	        .. code-block:: python
1554	
1555	            @mlflow.trace
1556	            def my_func(x):
1557	                mlflow.update_current_trace(tags={"fruit": "apple"}, client_request_id="req-12345")
1558	                return x + 1
1559	
1560	        Using within the ``with mlflow.start_span`` context manager:
1561	
1562	        .. code-block:: python
1563	
1564	            with mlflow.start_span("span"):
1565	                mlflow.update_current_trace(tags={"fruit": "apple"}, client_request_id="req-12345")
1566	
1567	        Updating user, session, and source information of the trace:
1568	
1569	        .. code-block:: python
1570	
1571	            mlflow.update_current_trace(
1572	                session_id="session-4f855da00427",
1573	                user="user-id-cc156f29bcfb",
1574	                metadata={
1575	                    "mlflow.source.name": "inference.py",
1576	                    "mlflow.source.git.commit": "1234567890",
1577	                    "mlflow.source.git.repoURL": "https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow",
1578	                },
1579	            )

1581	        Updating request preview:
1582	
1583	        .. code-block:: python
1584	
1585	            import mlflow
1586	            import openai
1587	
1588	
1589	            @mlflow.trace
1590	            def predict(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
1591	                # Customize the request preview to show the first and last messages
1592	                custom_preview = f"{messages[0]['content'][:10]} ... {messages[-1]['content'][:10]}"
1593	                mlflow.update_current_trace(request_preview=custom_preview)
1594

1596	                response = openai.chat.completions.create(

1600	
1601	                return response.choices[0].message.content

1604	            messages = [

1606	                {"role": "assistant", "content": "I'm good, thank you!"},
1607	                {"role": "user", "content": "What's your name?"},
1608	                # ... (long message history)
1609	                {"role": "assistant", "content": "Bye!"},
1610	            ]
1611	            predict(messages)
1612	
1613	            # The request preview rendered in the UI will be:
1614	            #     "Hi, how are you? ... Bye!"
1615	
1616	    """
1617	    active_span = get_current_active_span()
1618	
1619	    if not active_span:
1620	        _logger.warning(
1621	            "No active trace found. Please create a span using `mlflow.start_span` or "
1622	            "`@mlflow.trace` before calling `mlflow.update_current_trace`.",
1623	        )

1626	    def _warn_non_string_values(d: dict[str, Any], field_name: str):
1627	        if non_string_items := {k: v for k, v in d.items() if not isinstance(v, str)}:

1645	    _warn_non_string_values(metadata, "metadata")

1648	    # updating the backend store. The in-memory trace will be exported when it is ended.

1739	def add_trace(trace: Trace | dict[str, Any], target: LiveSpan | None = None):
1740	    """
1741	    Add a completed trace object into another trace.
1742	
1743	    This is particularly useful when you call a remote service instrumented by
1744	    MLflow Tracing. By using this function, you can merge the trace from the remote
1745	    service into the current active local trace, so that you can see the full
1746	    trace including what happens inside the remote service call.
1747	
1748	    The following example demonstrates how to use this function to merge a trace from a remote
1749	    service to the current active trace in the function.
1750	
1751	    .. code-block:: python
1752	
1753	        @mlflow.trace(name="predict")
1754	        def predict(input):
1755	            # Call a remote service that returns a trace in the response
1756	            resp = requests.get("https://your-service-endpoint", ...)
1757	
1758	            # Extract the trace from the response
1759	            trace_json = resp.json().get("trace")
1760	
1761	            # Use the remote trace as a part of the current active trace.
1762	            # It will be merged under the span "predict" and exported together when it is ended.
1763	            mlflow.add_trace(trace_json)
1764	
1765	    If you have a specific target span to merge the trace under, you can pass the target span
1766	
1767	    .. code-block:: python
1768	
1769	        def predict(input):
1770	            # Create a local span
1771	            with mlflow.start_span(name="predict") as span:
1772	                resp = requests.get("https://your-service-endpoint", ...)
1773	                trace_json = resp.json().get("trace")
1774	
1775	                # Merge the remote trace under the span created above
1776	                mlflow.add_trace(trace_json, target=span)
1777	
1778	    Args:
1779	        trace: A :py:class:`Trace <mlflow.entities.Trace>` object or a dictionary representation
1780	            of the trace. The trace **must** be already completed i.e. no further updates should
1781	            be made to it. Otherwise, this function will raise an exception.
1782	
1783	            .. attention:
1784	
1785	                The spans in the trace must be ordered in a way that the parent span comes
1786	                before its children. If the spans are not ordered correctly, this function
1787	                will raise an exception.
1788

1870	    """

1885	            When not specified, current time is used for start and end time of the trace.
1886	        execution_time_ms: The execution time of the trace in milliseconds since the UNIX epoch.

1892	
1893	    .. code-block:: python
1894	        :test:
1895	
1896	        import time
1897	        import mlflow
1898	
1899	        trace_id = mlflow.log_trace(
1900	            request="Does mlflow support tracing?",
1901	            response="Yes",
1902	            intermediate_outputs={
1903	                "retrieved_documents": ["mlflow documentation"],
1904	                "system_prompt": ["answer the question with yes or no"],
1905	            },
1906	            start_time_ms=int(time.time() * 1000),
1907	            execution_time_ms=5129,
1908	        )
1909	        trace = mlflow.get_trace(trace_id, flush=True)
1910	
1911	        print(trace.data.intermediate_outputs)

1913	    if intermediate_outputs:
1914	        if attributes:

1916	        else:
1917	            attributes = {SpanAttributeKey.INTERMEDIATE_OUTPUTS: intermediate_outputs}
1918	
1919	    span = start_span_no_context(
1920	        name=name,
1921	        inputs=request,
1922	        attributes=attributes,
1923	        tags=tags,
1924	        start_time_ns=start_time_ms * 1000000 if start_time_ms else None,
1925	    )

1936	def _merge_trace(
1937	    trace: Trace,
1938	    target_trace_id: str,
1939	    target_parent_span_id: str,
1940	):
1941	    """
1942	    Merge the given trace object under an existing trace in the in-memory trace registry.
1943	
1944	    Args:
1945	        trace: The trace object to be merged.
1946	        target_trace_id: The ID of the parent trace.
1947	        target_parent_span_id: The parent span ID, under which the child trace should be merged.
1948	    """
1949	    trace_manager = InMemoryTraceManager.get_instance()
1950	
1951	    # The merged trace should have the same trace ID as the parent trace.
1952	    with trace_manager.get_trace(target_trace_id) as parent_trace:
1953	        if not parent_trace:
1954	            _logger.warning(f"Parent trace with ID {target_trace_id} not found. Skipping merge.")
1955	            return
1956	
1957	        new_trace_id = parent_trace.span_dict[target_parent_span_id]._trace_id
1958	
1959	    for span in trace.data.spans:
1960	        parent_span_id = span.parent_id or target_parent_span_id
1961	
1962	        # NB: We clone span one by one in the order it was saved in the original trace. This
1963	        # works upon the assumption that the parent span always comes before its children.
1964	        # This is guaranteed in current implementation, but if it changes in the future,
1965	        # we have to traverse the tree to determine the order.
1966	        if not trace_manager.get_span_from_id(target_trace_id, parent_span_id):
1967	            raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
1968	                f"Span with ID {parent_span_id} not found. Please make sure the "
1969	                "spans in the trace are ordered correctly i.e. the parent span comes before "
1970	                "its children."
1971	            )
1972	
1973	        cloned_span = LiveSpan.from_immutable_span(
1974	            span=span,
1975	            parent_span_id=parent_span_id,
1976	            trace_id=target_trace_id,
1977	            otel_trace_id=new_trace_id,
1978	        )
1979	        trace_manager.register_span(cloned_span)
1980	        # end the cloned span to ensure it's processed by the exporter
1981	        cloned_span.end(end_time_ns=span.end_time_ns)
1982	
1983	    # Merge the tags and metadata from the child trace to the parent trace.
1984	    with trace_manager.get_trace(target_trace_id) as parent_trace:
1985	        # Order of merging is important to ensure the parent trace's metadata is
1986	        # not overwritten by the child trace's metadata if they have the same key.
1987	        parent_trace.info.tags = trace.info.tags | parent_trace.info.tags
1988	        parent_trace.info.trace_metadata = {
1989	            **trace.info.request_metadata,
1990	            **parent_trace.info.trace_metadata,
1991	        }

225	    """
226	    Client of an MLflow Tracking Server that creates and manages experiments and runs, and of an
227	    MLflow Registry Server that creates and manages registered models and model versions. It also
228	    exposes workspace CRUD via the configured workspace provider. It's a thin wrapper around:

237	    def __init__(
238	        self,

241	        workspace_store_uri: str | None = None,
242	    ):

246	                to the service set by ``mlflow.tracking.set_tracking_uri``. See
247	                `Where Runs Get Recorded <../tracking.html#where-runs-get-recorded>`_
248	                for more info.
249	            registry_uri: Address of local or remote model registry server. If not provided,
250	                defaults to the service set by ``mlflow.tracking.set_registry_uri``. If
251	                no such service was set, defaults to the tracking uri of the client.
252	            workspace_store_uri: Address of the workspace provider backend. Defaults to the tracking
253	                URI when unspecified, but can be pointed at a dedicated workspace store.
254	        """
255	        final_tracking_uri = utils._resolve_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
256	        self._registry_uri = registry_utils._resolve_registry_uri(registry_uri, tracking_uri)
257	        self._tracking_client = TrackingServiceClient(final_tracking_uri)
258	        self._workspace_store_uri = workspace_utils.resolve_workspace_store_uri(
259	            workspace_store_uri, tracking_uri=final_tracking_uri
260	        )

262	        self._workspace_client = None

264	        # `MlflowClient` also references a `ModelRegistryClient` instance that is provided by the
265	        # `MlflowClient._get_registry_client()` method. This `ModelRegistryClient` is not explicitly
266	        # defined as an instance variable in the `MlflowClient` constructor; an instance variable
267	        # is assigned lazily by `MlflowClient._get_registry_client()` and should not be referenced
268	        # outside of the `MlflowClient._get_registry_client()` method. The workspace provider client
269	        # follows the same lazy initialization pattern and is only constructed on demand via
270	        # `_get_workspace_client()`.

284	    def _get_registry_client(self):

289	            example, when the registry URI refers to an unsupported store type (e.g., the

294	        """
295	        # Attempt to fetch a `ModelRegistryClient` that is lazily instantiated and defined as
296	        # an instance variable on this `MlflowClient` instance. Because the instance variable
297	        # is undefined until the first invocation of _get_registry_client(), the `getattr()`
298	        # function is used to safely fetch the variable (if it is defined) or a NoneType
299	        # (if it is not defined)
300	        registry_client_attr = "_registry_client_lazy"
301	        registry_client = getattr(self, registry_client_attr, None)
302	        if registry_client is None:
303	            try:
304	                registry_client = ModelRegistryClient(self._registry_uri, self.tracking_uri)

487	
488	            # Create nested runs
489	            with mlflow.start_run():

640	    @require_prompt_registry
641	    @translate_prompt_exception
642	    def register_prompt(
643	        self,
644	        name: str,
645	        template: str | list[dict[str, Any]],
646	        commit_message: str | None = None,
647	        tags: dict[str, str] | None = None,
648	        response_format: type[BaseModel] | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
649	        model_config: "PromptModelConfig | dict[str, Any] | None" = None,
650	    ) -> PromptVersion:
651	        """
652	        Register a new :py:class:`Prompt <mlflow.entities.Prompt>` in the MLflow Prompt Registry.
653	
654	        A :py:class:`Prompt <mlflow.entities.Prompt>` is a pair of name
655	        and template content at minimum. With MLflow Prompt Registry, you can create, manage,
656	        and version control prompts with the MLflow's robust model tracking framework.
657	
658	        If there is no registered prompt with the given name, a new prompt will be created.
659	        Otherwise, a new version of the existing prompt will be created.
660	
661	        Example:
662	
663	        .. code-block:: python
664	
665	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
666	            from pydantic import BaseModel
667	
668	            # Your prompt registry URI
669	            client = MlflowClient(registry_uri="sqlite:///prompt_registry.db")
670	
671	            # Register a text prompt
672	            client.register_prompt(
673	                name="greeting_prompt",
674	                template="Respond to the user's message as a {{style}} AI.",
675	                response_format={"type": "string", "description": "A friendly response"},
676	            )
677	
678	            # Register a chat prompt with multiple messages
679	            client.register_prompt(
680	                name="assistant_prompt",
681	                template=[
682	                    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful {{style}} assistant."},
683	                    {"role": "user", "content": "{{question}}"},
684	                ],
685	                response_format={"type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string"}}},
686	            )
687	
688	            # Load the prompt from the registry
689	            prompt = client.load_prompt("greeting_prompt")
690	
691	            # Use the prompt in your application
692	            import openai
693	
694	            openai_client = openai.OpenAI()
695	            openai_client.chat.completion.create(
696	                model="gpt-4o-mini",
697	                messages=[
698	                    {"role": "system", "content": prompt.format(style="friendly")},
699	                    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello, how are you?"},
700	                ],
701	            )
702	
703	            # Update the prompt with a new version
704	            prompt = client.register_prompt(
705	                name="greeting_prompt",
706	                template="Respond to the user's message as a {{style}} AI. {{greeting}}",
707	                commit_message="Add a greeting to the prompt.",
708	                tags={"author": "Bob"},
709	            )
710	
711	        Args:
712	            name: The name of the prompt.
713	            template: The template content of the prompt. Can be either:
714	
715	                - A string containing text with variables enclosed in double curly braces,
716	                  e.g. {{variable}}, which will be replaced with actual values by the `format`
717	                  method.
718	                - A list of dictionaries representing chat messages, where each message has
719	                  'role' and 'content' keys (e.g., [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello {{name}}"}])
720	
721	            commit_message: A message describing the changes made to the prompt, similar to a
722	                Git commit message. Optional.
723	            tags: A dictionary of tags for the prompt.
724	                These tags are stored on the prompt version and written to prompt-level metadata.
725	                For OSS, later ``register_prompt()`` calls can overwrite the same keys at the
726	                prompt level. Optional.
727	            response_format: Optional Pydantic class or dictionary defining the expected response
728	                structure. This can be used to specify the schema for structured outputs from LLM
729	                calls.
730	            model_config: Optional PromptModelConfig instance or dictionary containing
731	                model-specific configuration like model_name, temperature, max_tokens, etc.
732	                Using PromptModelConfig provides validation and type safety.
733	
734	        Returns:
735	            A :py:class:`PromptVersion <mlflow.entities.PromptVersion>` object that was created.
736	        """
737	        registry_client = self._get_registry_client()
738	
739	        validate_prompt_name(name)
740	
741	        if is_databricks_unity_catalog_uri(self._registry_uri):
742	            try:
743	                registry_client.create_prompt(
744	                    name=name, description=commit_message, tags=tags or {}
745	                )
746	            except MlflowException as e:
747	                if e.error_code == ErrorCode.Name(ErrorCode.ALREADY_EXISTS):
748	                    pass
749	                else:
750	                    # Re-raise other errors like permission issues, validation errors, etc.
751	                    raise
752	
753	            # Create the prompt version
754	            prompt_version = registry_client.create_prompt_version(
755	                name=name,
756	                template=template,
757	                description=commit_message,
758	                tags=tags or {},
759	                response_format=response_format,
760	                model_config=model_config,
761	            )
762	
763	            prompt_version = registry_client.get_prompt_version(name, str(prompt_version.version))
764	            self._log_prompt_ui_link(name, prompt_version.version)
765	            return prompt_version
766	
767	        # OSS approach using RegisteredModel with special tags
768	        is_new_prompt = False
769	        rm = None
770	        tags = tags or {}
771	        try:
772	            rm = registry_client.get_registered_model(name)
773	        except MlflowException:
774	            # Create a new prompt (model) entry
775	            registry_client.create_registered_model(
776	                name, description=commit_message, tags={IS_PROMPT_TAG_KEY: "true", **tags}
777	            )
778	            is_new_prompt = True
779	
780	        # Check if the registered model is a prompt
781	        if rm and not has_prompt_tag(rm._tags):
782	            raise MlflowException(
783	                f"Model '{name}' exists with the same name. MLflow does not allow registering "
784	                "a prompt with the same name as an existing model. Please choose a different "
785	                "name for the prompt.",
786	                INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
787	            )
788	
789	        # Update the prompt tags
790	        if not is_new_prompt:
791	            for key, value in tags.items():
792	                registry_client.set_registered_model_tag(name, key, value)
793	
794	        # Version metadata is represented as ModelVersion tags in the registry
795	        tags = tags or {}
796	        tags.update({IS_PROMPT_TAG_KEY: "true"})
797	        if isinstance(template, list):
798	            tags.update({PROMPT_TYPE_TAG_KEY: PROMPT_TYPE_CHAT})
799	            tags.update({PROMPT_TEXT_TAG_KEY: json.dumps(template)})
800	        else:
801	            tags.update({PROMPT_TYPE_TAG_KEY: PROMPT_TYPE_TEXT})
802	            tags.update({PROMPT_TEXT_TAG_KEY: template})
803	        if response_format:
804	            tags.update({
805	                RESPONSE_FORMAT_TAG_KEY: json.dumps(
806	                    PromptVersion.convert_response_format_to_dict(response_format)
807	                ),
808	            })
809	        if model_config:
810	            # Convert ModelConfig to dict if needed
811	            if isinstance(model_config, PromptModelConfig):
812	                config_dict = model_config.to_dict()
813	            else:
814	                # Validate dict by converting through PromptModelConfig
815	                config_dict = PromptModelConfig.from_dict(model_config).to_dict()
816	
817	            tags.update({PROMPT_MODEL_CONFIG_TAG_KEY: json.dumps(config_dict)})
818	
819	        try:
820	            mv: ModelVersion = registry_client.create_model_version(
821	                name=name,
822	                description=commit_message,
823	                source=_CLIENT_PROMPT_SOURCE_PLACEHOLDER,  # Required field, unused for prompts
824	                tags=tags,
825	            )
826	        except Exception:
827	            if is_new_prompt:
828	                # When a model version creation fails for the first version of a prompt,
829	                # delete the registered model to avoid leaving a prompt with no versions
830	                registry_client.delete_registered_model(name)
831	            raise
832	
833	        # Fetch the prompt-level tags from the registered model
834	        prompt_tags = registry_client.get_registered_model(name)._tags
835	
836	        # Invalidate "latest" cache entry since we just created a new version
837	        PromptCache.get_instance().delete(name, alias="latest", registry_uri=self._registry_uri)
838	
839	        prompt_version = model_version_to_prompt_version(mv, prompt_tags=prompt_tags)
840	
841	        # Import here to avoid circular import
842	        from mlflow.tracking.fluent import _get_experiment_id
843	
844	        if experiment_id := _get_experiment_id():
845	            self._link_prompt_to_experiment(prompt_version, experiment_id)
846	
847	        return prompt_version
848	
849	    def _log_prompt_ui_link(self, name: str, version: int) -> None:
850	        """Log the registered prompt in the active experiment's Prompts tab.
851	
852	        Emits an informational message only; never raises.
853	        """
854	        try:
855	            workspace_url = get_workspace_url()
856	            # Import here to avoid circular import.
857	            from mlflow.tracking.fluent import _get_experiment_id
858	
859	            experiment_id = _get_experiment_id()
860	            if not workspace_url or not experiment_id:
861	                return
862	            parts = name.split(".")
863	            if len(parts) != 3:
864	                return
865	            workspace_id = get_workspace_id()
866	            query = (
867	                f"?o={workspace_id}&promptVersion={version}"
868	                if workspace_id
869	                else f"?promptVersion={version}"
870	            )
871	            _logger.info(
872	                "Prompt registered. View in experiment Prompts tab: "
873	                "%s/ml/experiments/%s/prompts/%s%s",
874	                workspace_url.rstrip("/"),
875	                experiment_id,
876	                name,
877	                query,
878	            )
879	        except Exception:
880	            _logger.debug("Failed to log prompt UI link", exc_info=True)

882	    def _link_prompt_to_experiment(self, prompt_version: PromptVersion, experiment_id: str) -> None:
883	        """
884	        Update the experiment IDs for a prompt version.
885	        """
886	
887	        def _link_prompt_to_experiment_async() -> None:
888	            try:
889	                with _prompt_experiment_link_lock:
890	                    prompt_info = self.get_prompt(prompt_version.name)
891	                    existing_ids = prompt_info.tags.get(PROMPT_EXPERIMENT_IDS_TAG_KEY, "")
892	                    existing_ids = existing_ids.rstrip(",").lstrip(",")
893	                    exp_ids = [eid.strip() for eid in existing_ids.split(",") if eid.strip()]
894	                    if experiment_id not in exp_ids:
895	                        exp_ids.append(experiment_id)
896	                        exp_ids = ",".join(exp_ids)
897	                        # Use LIKE to match the experiment ID and experiment ID is auto-incremented
898	                        # integer. So add comma before and after the list of experiment IDs to
899	                        # avoid false matches (e.g., "1" matches "10").
900	                        exp_ids = f",{exp_ids},"
901	                        self.set_prompt_tag(
902	                            name=prompt_version.name,
903	                            key=PROMPT_EXPERIMENT_IDS_TAG_KEY,
904	                            value=exp_ids,
905	                        )
906	            except Exception as e:
907	                _logger.warning(
908	                    f"Failed to tag prompt '{prompt_version.name}' with experiment ID "
909	                    f"{experiment_id}. Error: {e}",
910	                )
911	
912	        threading.Thread(
913	            target=_link_prompt_to_experiment_async,
914	            name=f"link_prompt_to_experiment_thread-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
915	        ).start()

919	    def search_prompts(
920	        self,
921	        filter_string: str | None = None,
922	        max_results: int = SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_DEFAULT,
923	        page_token: str | None = None,
924	        order_by: list[str] | None = None,
925	    ) -> PagedList[Prompt]:
926	        """
927	        Search for prompts in the MLflow Prompt Registry.
928	
929	        This call returns prompt metadata for prompts that have been marked
930	        as prompts (i.e. tagged with `mlflow.prompt.is_prompt=true`). We can
931	        further restrict results via a standard registry filter expression.
932	
933	        Args:
934	            filter_string (Optional[str]):
935	                An additional registry-search expression to apply (e.g.
936	                `"name LIKE 'my_prompt%'"`).  For Unity Catalog registries, must include
937	                catalog and schema: "catalog = 'catalog_name' AND schema = 'schema_name'".
938	            max_results (int):
939	                The maximum number of prompts to return in one page.  Defaults
940	                to `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_DEFAULT` (typically 1 000).
941	            page_token (Optional[str]):
942	                A pagination token from a previous `search_prompts` call; use this
943	                to retrieve the next page of results.  Defaults to `None`.
944	            order_by (Optional[list[str]]):
945	                List of column names with ASC|DESC annotation to order the results by.
946	                Not honored by Unity Catalog registries. Defaults to `None`.
947	
948	        Returns:
949	            A pageable list of :py:class:`Prompt <mlflow.entities.Prompt>` objects
950	            representing prompt metadata:
951	
952	            - name: The prompt name
953	            - description: The prompt description
954	            - tags: Prompt-level tags
955	            - creation_timestamp: When the prompt was created
956	
957	            To get the actual prompt template content,
958	            use get_prompt_version() with a specific version:
959	
960	            .. code-block:: python
961	
962	                from mlflow import MlflowClient
963	
964	                # Your prompt registry URI
965	                client = MlflowClient(registry_uri="sqlite:///prompt_registry.db")
966	
967	                # Search for prompts
968	                prompts = client.search_prompts(filter_string="name LIKE 'greeting%'")
969	
970	                # Get prompts by experiment

995	    def load_prompt(
996	        self,
997	        name_or_uri: str,
998	        version: str | int | None = None,
999	        allow_missing: bool = False,
1000	        cache_ttl_seconds: float | None = None,
1001	    ) -> PromptVersion | None:
1002	        """
1003	        Load a :py:class:`Prompt <mlflow.entities.Prompt>` from the MLflow Prompt Registry.
1004	
1005	        The prompt can be specified by name and version, or by URI.
1006	
1007	        Example:
1008	
1009	        .. code-block:: python
1010	
1011	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
1012	
1013	            client = MlflowClient(registry_uri="sqlite:///prompt_registry.db")
1014	
1015	            # Load a specific version of the prompt by name and version
1016	            prompt = client.load_prompt("my_prompt", version=1)
1017	
1018	            # Load a specific version of the prompt by URI
1019	            prompt = client.load_prompt("prompts:/my_prompt/1")
1020	
1021	        Args:
1022	            name_or_uri: The name of the prompt, or the URI in the format "prompts:/name/version".
1023	            version: The version of the prompt (required when using name, not allowed when
1024	                using URI).
1025	            allow_missing: If True, return None instead of raising Exception if the specified prompt
1026	                is not found.
1027	            cache_ttl_seconds: Time-to-live for caching the prompt in seconds. If None, uses
1028	                the value from `MLFLOW_ALIAS_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` environment variable for
1029	                alias-based prompts (default 60), and the value from
1030	                `MLFLOW_VERSION_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` environment variable for version-based
1031	                prompts (default None, no TTL). Set to 0 to disable caching.
1032	        """
1033	        prompt_uri = parse_prompt_name_or_uri(name_or_uri, version)
1034	
1035	        if cache_ttl_seconds is None:
1036	            cache_ttl_seconds = (
1037	                MLFLOW_ALIAS_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.get()
1038	                if "@" in prompt_uri
1039	                else MLFLOW_VERSION_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.get()
1040	            )
1041	        if cache_ttl_seconds < 0:
1042	            raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
1043	                "`cache_ttl_seconds` argument must be greater than or equal to 0.",
1044	            )
1045	
1046	        # Check cache if cache_ttl_seconds > 0 (0 means no caching)
1047	        if cache_ttl_seconds > 0:
1048	            cache = PromptCache.get_instance()
1049	            cache_key = PromptCacheKey.from_uri(prompt_uri, registry_uri=self._registry_uri)
1050	            if cached_prompt := cache.get(cache_key):
1051	                return cached_prompt
1052	
1053	        # Fetch from server
1054	        try:
1055	            name, version_or_alias = self.parse_prompt_uri(prompt_uri)
1056	            registry_client = self._get_registry_client()
1057	            if isinstance(version_or_alias, str) and not version_or_alias.isdigit():
1058	                prompt = registry_client.get_prompt_version_by_alias(name, version_or_alias)
1059	            else:
1060	                prompt = registry_client.get_prompt_version(name, version_or_alias)
1061	
1062	            # Link the prompt to the active experiment. This is called only when
1063	            # the prompt is loaded from the registry to avoid performance overhead.
1064	            # Import here to avoid circular import
1065	            from mlflow.tracking.fluent import _get_experiment_id
1066	
1067	            if prompt and (experiment_id := _get_experiment_id()):
1068	                self._link_prompt_to_experiment(prompt, experiment_id)
1069	
1070	            # Cache the result if cache_ttl_seconds > 0
1071	            # `ttl_seconds=None` means cache with no TTL
1072	            if prompt and cache_ttl_seconds > 0:
1073	                cache.set(cache_key, prompt, ttl_seconds=cache_ttl_seconds)
1074	
1075	            return prompt
1076	        except MlflowException as exc:
1077	            if allow_missing and exc.error_code in (
1078	                ErrorCode.Name(RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST),
1079	                ErrorCode.Name(INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE),  # Missing alias (file/sql registry only)
1080	                ErrorCode.Name(NOT_FOUND),
1081	            ):
1082	                return None
1083	            raise

1341	    def parse_prompt_uri(self, uri: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
1342	        """
1343	        Parse prompt URI into prompt name and prompt version.
1344	        - 'prompts:/<name>/<version>' -> ('<name>', '<version>')
1345	        - 'prompts:/<name>@<alias>' -> ('<name>', '<version>')
1346	
1347	        This method reuses the existing model URI parsing logic with prompts prefix.
1348	        """
1349	        # Use the existing model URI parsing utilities with prompts scheme
1350	        parsed_prompt_uri = _parse_model_uri(uri, scheme="prompts")
1351	
1352	        if parsed_prompt_uri.model_id is not None:
1353	            # This shouldn't happen for prompts (no model IDs), but handle gracefully
1354	            raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(f"Invalid prompt URI format: {uri}")
1355	
1356	        if parsed_prompt_uri.version is not None:
1357	            # Direct version reference: prompts:/name/version
1358	            return parsed_prompt_uri.name, parsed_prompt_uri.version
1359	
1360	        if parsed_prompt_uri.alias is not None:
1361	            # Alias reference: prompts:/name@alias - resolve to version
1362	            prompt_version = self.get_prompt_version_by_alias(
1363	                parsed_prompt_uri.name, parsed_prompt_uri.alias
1364	            )
1365	            return parsed_prompt_uri.name, str(prompt_version.version)
1366	
1367	        # Handle stage or latest (not supported for prompts)
1368	        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
1369	            f"Invalid prompt URI: {uri}. Prompts do not support stage-based references."
1370	        )

1532	        self,
1533	        name: str,

1536	        attributes: dict[str, str] | None = None,

1541	        links: list[Link] | None = None,

1543	        """
1544	        Create a new trace object and start a root span under it.
1545	
1546	        This is an imperative API to manually create a new span under a specific trace id and
1547	        parent span, unlike the higher-level APIs like :py:func:`@mlflow.trace <mlflow.trace>`
1548	        and :py:func:`with mlflow.start_span() <mlflow.start_span>`, which automatically manage
1549	        the span lifecycle and parent-child relationship. You only need to call this method
1550	        when using the :py:func:`start_span() <start_span>` method of MlflowClient to create
1551	        spans.
1552	
1553	        .. attention::
1554	
1555	            A trace started with this method must be ended by calling
1556	            ``MlflowClient().end_trace(trace_id)``. Otherwise the trace will be not recorded.
1557	
1558	        Args:
1559	            name: The name of the trace (and the root span).
1560	            span_type: The type of the span.
1561	            inputs: Inputs to set on the root span of the trace.
1562	            attributes: A dictionary of attributes to set on the root span of the trace.
1563	            tags: A dictionary of tags to set on the trace.
1564	            experiment_id: The ID of the experiment to create the trace in. If not provided,
1565	                MLflow will look for valid experiment in the following order: activated using
1566	                :py:func:`mlflow.set_experiment() <mlflow.set_experiment>`,
1567	                ``MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME`` environment variable, ``MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID``
1568	                environment variable, or the default experiment as defined by the tracking server.
1569	            start_time_ns: The start time of the trace in nanoseconds since the UNIX epoch.
1570	            run_id: The ID of the MLflow run to associate with the trace. If provided, the
1571	                trace will be linked to this run.
1572	            links: A list of :py:class:`Link <mlflow.entities.Link>` objects to associate with
1573	                the root span.
1574

1576	            An :py:class:`Span <mlflow.entities.Span>` object
1577	            representing the root span of the trace.
1578	
1579	        Example:
1580	
1581	        .. code-block:: python
1582	            :test:
1583	
1584	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
1585	
1586	            client = MlflowClient()
1587	
1588	            root_span = client.start_trace("my_trace")
1589	            trace_id = root_span.trace_id
1590	
1591	            # Create a child span
1592	            child_span = client.start_span(
1593	                "child_span", trace_id=trace_id, parent_id=root_span.span_id
1594	            )
1595	            # Do something...
1596	            client.end_span(trace_id=trace_id, span_id=child_span.span_id)
1597	
1598	            client.end_trace(trace_id)
1599	        """
1600	        # Validate no active trace is set in the global context. If there is an active trace,
1601	        # the span created by this method will be a child span under the active trace rather than
1602	        # a root span of a new trace, which is not desired behavior.
1603	        if span := mlflow.get_current_active_span():
1604	            raise MlflowException(
1605	                f"Another trace is already set in the global context with ID {span.trace_id}. "
1606	                "It appears that you have already started a trace using fluent APIs like "
1607	                "`@mlflow.trace()` or `with mlflow.start_span()`. However, it is not allowed "
1608	                "to call MlflowClient.start_trace() under an active trace created by fluent APIs "
1609	                "because it may lead to unexpected behavior. To resolve this issue, consider the "
1610	                "following options:\n"
1611	                " - To create a child span under the active trace, use "
1612	                "`with mlflow.start_span()` or `MlflowClient.start_span()` instead.\n"
1613	                " - To start multiple traces in parallel, avoid using fluent APIs "
1614	                "and create all traces using `MlflowClient.start_trace()`.",
1615	                error_code=BAD_REQUEST,
1616	            )
1617	        metadata = {TraceMetadataKey.SOURCE_RUN: run_id} if run_id is not None else None
1618	
1619	        return start_span_no_context(
1620	            name=name,
1621	            span_type=span_type,
1622	            inputs=inputs,
1623	            attributes=attributes,
1624	            tags=tags,
1625	            metadata=metadata,
1626	            experiment_id=experiment_id,
1627	            start_time_ns=start_time_ns,
1628	            links=links,
1629	        )

1709	        inputs: Any | None = None,

1714	        """
1715	        Create a new span and start it without attaching it to the global trace context.
1716	
1717	        This is an imperative API to manually create a new span under a specific trace id
1718	        and parent span, unlike the higher-level APIs like
1719	        :py:func:`@mlflow.trace <mlflow.trace>` decorator and
1720	        :py:func:`with mlflow.start_span() <mlflow.start_span>` context manager, which
1721	        automatically manage the span lifecycle and parent-child relationship.
1722	
1723	        This API is useful for the case where the automatic context management is not
1724	        sufficient, such as callback-based instrumentation where span start and end are
1725	        not in the same call stack, or multi-threaded applications where the context is
1726	        not propagated automatically.
1727	
1728	        This API requires a parent span ID to be provided explicitly. If you haven't
1729	        started any span yet, use the :py:func:`start_trace() <start_trace>` method to
1730	        start a new trace and a root span.
1731	
1732	        .. warning::
1733	
1734	            The span created with this method needs to be ended explicitly by calling
1735	            the :py:func:`end_span() <end_span>` method. Otherwise the span will be
1736	            recorded with the incorrect end time and status ``TRACE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED``.
1737	
1738	        .. tip::
1739	
1740	            Instead of creating a root span with the :py:func:`start_trace() <start_trace>`
1741	            method, you can also use this method within the context of a parent span created
1742	            by the fluent APIs like :py:func:`@mlflow.trace <mlflow.trace>` and
1743	            :py:func:`with mlflow.start_span() <mlflow.start_span>`, by passing its span
1744	            ids the parent. This flexibility allows you to use the imperative APIs in
1745	            conjunction with the fluent APIs like below:
1746	
1747	            .. code-block:: python
1748	                :test:
1749	
1750	                import mlflow
1751	                from mlflow import MlflowClient
1752	
1753	                client = MlflowClient()
1754	
1755	                with mlflow.start_span("parent_span") as parent_span:
1756	                    child_span = client.start_span(
1757	                        name="child_span",
1758	                        trace_id=parent_span.trace_id,
1759	                        parent_id=parent_span.span_id,
1760	                    )
1761	
1762	                    # Do something...
1763	
1764	                    client.end_span(
1765	                        trace_id=parent_span.trace_id,
1766	                        span_id=child_span.span_id,
1767	                    )
1768	
1769	            However, **the opposite does not work**. You cannot use the fluent APIs within
1770	            the span created by this MlflowClient API. This is because the fluent APIs
1771	            fetches the current span from the managed context, which is not set by the MLflow
1772	            Client APIs. Once you create a span with the MLflow Client APIs, all children
1773	            spans must be created with the MLflow Client APIs. Please be cautious when using
1774	            this mixed approach, as it can lead to unexpected behavior if not used properly.
1775	
1776	        Args:
1777	            name: The name of the span.
1778	            trace_id: The ID of the trace to attach the span to. This is synonym to
1779	                trace_id` in OpenTelemetry.
1780	            parent_id: The ID of the parent span. The parent span can be a span created by
1781	                both fluent APIs like `with mlflow.start_span()`, and imperative APIs like this.
1782	            span_type: The type of the span. Can be either a string or a
1783	                :py:class:`SpanType <mlflow.entities.SpanType>` enum value.
1784	            inputs: Inputs to set on the span.
1785	            attributes: A dictionary of attributes to set on the span.
1786	            start_time_ns: The start time of the span in nano seconds since the UNIX epoch.
1787	                If not provided, the current time will be used.
1788	            links: A list of :py:class:`Link <mlflow.entities.Link>` objects to associate with
1789	                the span.
1790	
1791	        Returns:
1792	            An :py:class:`mlflow.entities.Span` object representing the span.
1793	
1794	        Example:
1795	
1796	        .. code-block:: python
1797	            :test:
1798	
1799	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
1800	
1801	            client = MlflowClient()
1802	
1803	            span = client.start_trace("my_trace")
1804	
1805	            x = 2
1806	
1807	            # Create a child span
1808	            child_span = client.start_span(
1809	                "child_span",
1810	                trace_id=span.trace_id,
1811	                parent_id=span.span_id,
1812	                inputs={"x": x},
1813	            )
1814	
1815	            y = x**2
1816	
1817	            client.end_span(
1818	                trace_id=child_span.trace_id,
1819	                span_id=child_span.span_id,
1820	                attributes={"factor": 2},
1821	                outputs={"y": y},
1822	            )
1823	
1824	            client.end_trace(span.trace_id)
1825	        """
1826	        # If parent span is no-op span, the child should also be no-op too
1827	        if trace_id == NO_OP_SPAN_TRACE_ID:
1828	            return NoOpSpan()
1829	
1830	        if not parent_id:
1831	            raise MlflowException(
1832	                "start_span() must be called with an explicit parent_id."
1833	                "If you haven't started any span yet, use MLflowClient().start_trace() "
1834	                "to start a new trace and root span.",
1835	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
1836	            )
1837	        if not trace_id:
1838	            raise MlflowException(
1839	                "Trace ID must be provided to start a span.",
1840	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
1841	            )
1842	
1843	        trace_manager = InMemoryTraceManager.get_instance()
1844	        if not (parent_span := trace_manager.get_span_from_id(trace_id, parent_id)):
1845	            raise MlflowException(
1846	                f"Parent span with ID '{parent_id}' not found.",
1847	                error_code=RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST,
1848	            )
1849	
1850	        return start_span_no_context(
1851	            name=name,
1852	            span_type=span_type,
1853	            parent_span=parent_span,
1854	            inputs=inputs,
1855	            attributes=attributes,
1856	            start_time_ns=start_time_ns,
1857	            links=links,
1858	        )

1952	    def search_experiments(
1953	        self,
1954	        view_type: int = ViewType.ACTIVE_ONLY,
1955	        max_results: int | None = SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_DEFAULT,
1956	        filter_string: str | None = None,
1957	        order_by: list[str] | None = None,
1958	        page_token=None,
1959	    ) -> PagedList[Experiment]:
1960	        """
1961	        Search for experiments that match the specified search query.
1962	
1963	        Args:
1964	            view_type: One of enum values ``ACTIVE_ONLY``, ``DELETED_ONLY``, or ``ALL``
1965	                defined in :py:class:`mlflow.entities.ViewType`.
1966	            max_results: Maximum number of experiments desired. Certain server backend may apply
1967	                its own limit.
1968	            filter_string: Filter query string (e.g., ``"name = 'my_experiment'"``), defaults to
1969	                searching for all experiments. The following identifiers, comparators, and logical
1970	                operators are supported.
1971	
1972	                Identifiers
1973	                  - ``name``: Experiment name
1974	                  - ``creation_time``: Experiment creation time
1975	                  - ``last_update_time``: Experiment last update time
1976	                  - ``tags.<tag_key>``: Experiment tag. If ``tag_key`` contains
1977	                    spaces, it must be wrapped with backticks (e.g., ``"tags.`extra key`"``).
1978	
1979	                Comparators for string attributes and tags
1980	                  - ``=``: Equal to
1981	                  - ``!=``: Not equal to
1982	                  - ``LIKE``: Case-sensitive pattern match
1983	                  - ``ILIKE``: Case-insensitive pattern match
1984	
1985	                Comparators for numeric attributes
1986	                  - ``=``: Equal to
1987	                  - ``!=``: Not equal to
1988	                  - ``<``: Less than
1989	                  - ``<=``: Less than or equal to
1990	                  - ``>``: Greater than
1991	                  - ``>=``: Greater than or equal to
1992	
1993	                Logical operators
1994	                  - ``AND``: Combines two sub-queries and returns True if both of them are True.
1995	
1996	            order_by: List of columns to order by. The ``order_by`` column can contain an optional
1997	                ``DESC`` or ``ASC`` value (e.g., ``"name DESC"``). The default ordering is ``ASC``,
1998	                so ``"name"`` is equivalent to ``"name ASC"``. If unspecified, defaults to
1999	                ``["last_update_time DESC"]``, which lists experiments updated most recently first.
2000	                The following fields are supported:
2001	
2002	                - ``experiment_id``: Experiment ID
2003	                - ``name``: Experiment name
2004	                - ``creation_time``: Experiment creation time
2005	                - ``last_update_time``: Experiment last update time
2006	
2007	            page_token: Token specifying the next page of results. It should be obtained from
2008	                a ``search_experiments`` call.
2009	
2010	        Returns:
2011	            A :py:class:`PagedList <mlflow.store.entities.PagedList>` of
2012	            :py:class:`Experiment <mlflow.entities.Experiment>` objects. The pagination token
2013	            for the next page can be obtained via the ``token`` attribute of the object.
2014	
2015	        .. code-block:: python
2016	            :caption: Example
2017	
2018	            import mlflow
2019	
2020	
2021	            def assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, expected_names):
2022	                actual_names = [e.name for e in experiments if e.name != "Default"]
2023	                assert actual_names == expected_names, (actual_names, expected_names)
2024	
2025	
2026	            mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///:memory:")
2027	            client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
2028	
2029	            # Create experiments
2030	            for name, tags in [
2031	                ("a", None),
2032	                ("b", None),
2033	                ("ab", {"k": "v"}),
2034	                ("bb", {"k": "V"}),
2035	            ]:
2036	                client.create_experiment(name, tags=tags)
2037	
2038	            # Search for experiments with name "a"
2039	            experiments = client.search_experiments(filter_string="name = 'a'")
2040	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["a"])
2041	
2042	            # Search for experiments with name starting with "a"
2043	            experiments = client.search_experiments(filter_string="name LIKE 'a%'")
2044	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["ab", "a"])
2045	
2046	            # Search for experiments with tag key "k" and value ending with "v" or "V"
2047	            experiments = client.search_experiments(filter_string="tags.k ILIKE '%v'")
2048	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["bb", "ab"])
2049	
2050	            # Search for experiments with name ending with "b" and tag {"k": "v"}
2051	            experiments = client.search_experiments(filter_string="name LIKE '%b' AND tags.k = 'v'")
2052	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["ab"])
2053	
2054	            # Sort experiments by name in ascending order
2055	            experiments = client.search_experiments(order_by=["name"])
2056	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["a", "ab", "b", "bb"])
2057	
2058	            # Sort experiments by ID in descending order
2059	            experiments = client.search_experiments(order_by=["experiment_id DESC"])
2060	            assert_experiment_names_equal(experiments, ["bb", "ab", "b", "a"])
2061	        """
2062	        return self._tracking_client.search_experiments(
2063	            view_type=view_type,

2335	        """
2336	        Log a metric against the run ID.
2337	
2338	        Args:
2339	            run_id: The run id to which the metric should be logged.
2340	            key: Metric name. This string may only contain alphanumerics, underscores
2341	                (_), dashes (-), periods (.), spaces ( ), and slashes (/).
2342	                All backend stores will support keys up to length 250, but some may
2343	                support larger keys.
2344	            value: Metric value. Note that some special values such
2345	                as +/- Infinity may be replaced by other values depending on the store. For
2346	                example, the SQLAlchemy store replaces +/- Inf with max / min float values.
2347	                All backend stores will support values up to length 5000, but some
2348	                may support larger values.
2349	            timestamp: Time when this metric was calculated. Defaults to the current system time.
2350	            step: Integer training step (iteration) at which was the metric calculated.
2351	                Defaults to 0.
2352	            synchronous: *Experimental* If True, blocks until the metric is logged successfully.
2353	                If False, logs the metric asynchronously and returns a future representing the
2354	                logging operation. If None, read from environment variable
2355	                `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_LOGGING`, which defaults to False if not set.
2356	            dataset_name: The name of the dataset associated with the metric. If specified,
2357	                ``dataset_digest`` must also be provided.
2358	            dataset_digest: The digest of the dataset associated with the metric. If specified,
2359	                ``dataset_name`` must also be provided.
2360	            model_id: The ID of the model associated with the metric. If not specified, use the
2361	                current active model ID set by :py:func:`mlflow.set_active_model`.
2362	
2363	        Returns:
2364	            When `synchronous=True` or None, returns None. When `synchronous=False`, returns an
2365	            :py:class:`mlflow.utils.async_logging.run_operations.RunOperations` instance that
2366	            represents future for logging operation.

2368	        .. code-block:: python
2369	            :caption: Example
2370	
2371	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
2372	
2373	
2374	            def print_run_info(r):
2375	                print(f"run_id: {r.info.run_id}")
2376	                print(f"metrics: {r.data.metrics}")
2377	                print(f"status: {r.info.status}")
2378	
2379	
2380	            # Create a run under the default experiment (whose id is '0').
2381	            # Since these are low-level CRUD operations, this method will create a run.
2382	            # To end the run, you'll have to explicitly end it.
2383	            client = MlflowClient()
2384	            experiment_id = "0"
2385	            run = client.create_run(experiment_id)
2386	            print_run_info(run)
2387	            print("--")
2388	
2389	            # Log the metric. Unlike mlflow.log_metric this method
2390	            # does not start a run if one does not exist. It will log
2391	            # the metric for the run id in the backend store.
2392	            client.log_metric(run.info.run_id, "m", 1.5)
2393	            client.set_terminated(run.info.run_id)
2394	            run = client.get_run(run.info.run_id)
2395	            print_run_info(run)

2712	    def log_batch(
2713	        self,
2714	        run_id: str,
2715	        metrics: Sequence[Metric] = (),
2716	        params: Sequence[Param] = (),
2717	        tags: Sequence[RunTag] = (),
2718	        synchronous: bool | None = None,
2719	    ) -> RunOperations | None:
2720	        """
2721	        Log multiple metrics, params, and/or tags.
2722	
2723	        Args:
2724	            run_id: String ID of the run
2725	            metrics: If provided, List of Metric(key, value, timestamp) instances.
2726	            params: If provided, List of Param(key, value) instances.
2727	            tags: If provided, List of RunTag(key, value) instances.
2728	            synchronous: *Experimental* If True, blocks until the metric is logged successfully.
2729	                If False, logs the metric asynchronously and returns a future representing the
2730	                logging operation. If None, read from environment variable
2731	                `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_LOGGING`, which defaults to False if not set.
2732	
2733	        Raises:
2734	            mlflow.MlflowException: If any errors occur.
2735	
2736	        Returns:
2737	            When `synchronous=True` or None, returns None. When `synchronous=False`, returns an
2738	            :py:class:`mlflow.utils.async_logging.run_operations.RunOperations` instance that
2739	            represents future for logging operation.
2740	
2741	        .. code-block:: python
2742	            :caption: Example
2743	
2744	            import time
2745	
2746	            from mlflow import MlflowClient
2747	            from mlflow.entities import Metric, Param, RunTag
2748	
2749	
2750	            def print_run_info(r):
2751	                print(f"run_id: {r.info.run_id}")
2752	                print(f"params: {r.data.params}")
2753	                print(f"metrics: {r.data.metrics}")
2754	                print(f"tags: {r.data.tags}")
2755	                print(f"status: {r.info.status}")
2756	
2757	
2758	            # Create MLflow entities and a run under the default experiment (whose id is '0').
2759	            timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
2760	            metrics = [Metric("m", 1.5, timestamp, 1)]
2761	            params = [Param("p", "p")]
2762	            tags = [RunTag("t", "t")]
2763	            experiment_id = "0"
2764	            client = MlflowClient()
2765	            run = client.create_run(experiment_id)
2766	
2767	            # Log entities, terminate the run, and fetch run status
2768	            client.log_batch(run.info.run_id, metrics=metrics, params=params, tags=tags)
2769	            client.set_terminated(run.info.run_id)
2770	            run = client.get_run(run.info.run_id)
2771	            print_run_info(run)
2772	
2773	            # To log metric in async fashion
2774	            client.log_metric(run.info.run_id, "m", 1.5, synchronous=False)
2775	
2776	        .. code-block:: text
2777	            :caption: Output
2778	
2779	            run_id: ef0247fa3205410595acc0f30f620871
2780	            params: {'p': 'p'}
2781	            metrics: {'m': 1.5}
2782	            tags: {'t': 't'}
2783	            status: FINISHED
2784	
2785	        """
2786	        synchronous = (
2787	            synchronous if synchronous is not None else not MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_LOGGING.get()
2788	        )
2789	
2790	        # Stringify the values of the params
2791	        params = [Param(key=param.key, value=str(param.value)) for param in params]
2792	
2793	        return self._tracking_client.log_batch(
2794	            run_id, metrics, params, tags, synchronous=synchronous
2795	        )

2913	    def _log_artifact_helper(self, run_id, artifact_file):

2930	            yield tmp_path

5257	                  - ``IN``: In a value list. Only ``run_id`` identifier supports ``IN`` comparator.

6398	        deleted first before the prompt itself can be deleted.

6402	        Args:

6404	
6405	        Example:
6406

6410	
6411	            client = MlflowClient()
6412	
6413	            # For Unity Catalog, delete all versions first
6414	            if client.get_registry_uri().startswith("databricks-uc"):
6415	                versions = client.search_prompt_versions("my_prompt")
6416	                for version in versions:
6417	                    client.delete_prompt_version("my_prompt", version.version)
6418	
6419	            # Then delete the prompt
6420	            client.delete_prompt("my_prompt")
6421	        """
6422	        registry_client = self._get_registry_client()
6423	
6424	        # Only check for existing versions in Unity Catalog registries
6425	        registry_uri = self._registry_uri
6426	
6427	        if is_databricks_unity_catalog_uri(registry_uri):
6428	            versions = self.search_prompt_versions(name, max_results=1)
6429	
6430	            if len(versions) > 0:
6431	                raise MlflowException(

6433	                    f"Please delete all versions first using delete_prompt_version(), "

6436	                )

6439	        # that may be updating tags on this prompt. This prevents race conditions where
6440	        # the background thread holds a session open while we try to delete.
6441	        with _prompt_experiment_link_lock:

import mimetypes
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlencode, urlparse


class Attachment:
    """
    Represents a binary attachment (image, audio, PDF, etc.) that can be logged
    as part of a trace span's inputs or outputs.

    When an Attachment is set as a span input/output value, it is automatically:
    1. Replaced with a reference URI in the span data
    2. Uploaded as a separate artifact file alongside the trace data
    """

    def __init__(self, *, content_type: str, content_bytes: bytes):
        self._id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        self._content_type = content_type
        self._content_bytes = content_bytes

    @classmethod
    def from_file(cls, path: str | Path, content_type: str | None = None) -> "Attachment":
        path = Path(path)
        if content_type is None:
            guessed, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(str(path))
            content_type = guessed or "application/octet-stream"
        return cls(content_type=content_type, content_bytes=path.read_bytes())

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        return self._id

    @property
    def content_type(self) -> str:
        return self._content_type

    @property
    def content_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return self._content_bytes

    def ref(self, trace_id: str) -> str:
        query = urlencode({
            "content_type": self._content_type,
            "trace_id": trace_id,
            "size": str(len(self._content_bytes)),
        })
        return f"mlflow-attachment://{self._id}?{query}"

    @staticmethod
    def parse_ref(ref_uri: str) -> dict[str, str | int | None] | None:
        parsed = urlparse(ref_uri)
        if parsed.scheme != "mlflow-attachment":
            return None
        params = parse_qs(parsed.query)
        attachment_id = parsed.hostname
        content_type = params.get("content_type", [None])[0]
        trace_id = params.get("trace_id", [None])[0]
        if not attachment_id or not content_type or not trace_id:
            return None
        size_str = params.get("size", [None])[0]
        try:
            size = int(size_str) if size_str else None
        except ValueError:
            size = None
        if size is not None and size <= 0:
            size = None
        return {
            "attachment_id": attachment_id,
            "content_type": content_type,
            "trace_id": trace_id,
            "size": size,
        }

    from mlflow.entities.link import Link

    trace_id = "tr-12345"
    tracer = _get_tracer("test")
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("test_span") as otel_span:

        live_span.add_link(
            Link(trace_id="tr-abc", span_id="aabbccddeeff0011", attributes={"k": "v"})

def test_lazy_span_to_dict_does_not_materialize():
    from mlflow.entities.span import LazySpan

    with mlflow.start_span("parent"):
        with mlflow.start_span("child", span_type=SpanType.LLM) as span:
            span.set_inputs({"input": 1})
            span.set_outputs(2)

    span_dict = span.to_dict()
    lazy = LazySpan(span_dict)

    assert isinstance(lazy, Span)
    assert not isinstance(lazy, LiveSpan)
    assert lazy.to_dict() is span_dict
    assert lazy.__dict__["_materialized"] is False


def test_lazy_span_materializes_on_property_access():
    from mlflow.entities.span import LazySpan

    with mlflow.start_span("parent"):
        with mlflow.start_span("child", span_type=SpanType.LLM) as span:
            span.set_inputs({"input": 1})
            span.set_outputs(2)
            span.set_status("OK")

    span_dict = span.to_dict()
    lazy = LazySpan(span_dict)

    assert lazy.name == "child"
    assert lazy.__dict__["_materialized"] is True

def test_lazy_span_matches_eager_span_after_materialization():
    from mlflow.entities.link import Link
    from mlflow.entities.span import LazySpan
    from mlflow.tracing.otel.translation import translate_loaded_span

    trace_id = "tr-12345"
    tracer = _get_tracer("test")
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("parent"):
        with tracer.start_as_current_span("child") as otel_span:
            span = create_mlflow_span(otel_span, trace_id=trace_id, span_type=SpanType.LLM)
            span.set_inputs({"input": 1})
            span.set_outputs({"output": 2})
            span.set_status("OK")
            span.add_event(SpanEvent("test_event", timestamp=0, attributes={"foo": "bar"}))
            span.add_link(
                Link(trace_id="tr-abc123", span_id="aabbccddeeff0011", attributes={"type": "test"})

    span_dict = translate_loaded_span(span.to_dict())
    eager = Span.from_dict(span_dict)

    assert lazy.to_dict() == eager.to_dict()
    assert lazy.to_otel_proto().SerializeToString() == eager.to_otel_proto().SerializeToString()

    _ = lazy.name
    assert lazy.__dict__["_materialized"] is True
    assert lazy.to_dict() == eager.to_dict()
    assert lazy.attributes == eager.attributes
    assert lazy.links == eager.links
    assert lazy.status == eager.status
    assert lazy.events == eager.events
    assert lazy.to_otel_proto().SerializeToString() == eager.to_otel_proto().SerializeToString()

346	    # serialized through its dict form instead.

364	    def __deepcopy__(self, memo: dict[int, Any]):

384	            "trace_id": _encode_bytes_to_base64(

390	            )
391	            if self._span.parent

397	                {
398	                    "name": event.name,
399	                    "time_unix_nano": event.timestamp,
400	                    "attributes": event.attributes,

409	            # Read raw values directly from the OTel span to skip a full json.loads pass
