415	    @classmethod
416	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "Span":
417	        """Create a Span object from the given dictionary."""
418	        try:
419	            # Try to deserialize the span using the v3 schema
420	            request_id = data.get("attributes", {}).get(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID)
421	            if not request_id:
422	                raise MlflowException(
423	                    f"The {SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID} attribute is empty or missing.",
424	                    INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
425	                )
426	
427	            if Span._is_span_v2_schema(data):
428	                return cls.from_dict_v2(data)
429	
430	            if _is_base64_encoded(data["trace_id"]):
431	                otel_trace_id = _decode_id_from_byte(data["trace_id"])
432	                span_id = _decode_id_from_byte(data["span_id"])
433	                # Parent ID always exists in proto (empty string) even if the span is a root span.
434	                parent_id = (
435	                    _decode_id_from_byte(data["parent_span_id"]) if data["parent_span_id"] else None
436	                )
437	            else:
438	                # In 3.5.0, Span.to_dict keeps trace_id and span_id as the object's properties
439	                # format, so we need special handling for it.
440	                otel_trace_id = decode_id(
441	                    parse_trace_id_v4(data["trace_id"])[1].removeprefix(TRACE_REQUEST_ID_PREFIX)
442	                )
443	                span_id = decode_id(data["span_id"])
444	                parent_id = decode_id(data["parent_span_id"]) if data["parent_span_id"] else None
445	
446	            status_code_str = data["status"]["code"]
447	            try:
448	                status_code = SpanStatusCode.from_otel_proto_status_code_name(status_code_str)
449	            except MlflowException:
450	                # In 3.5.0 Span.to_dict keeps status code as the SpanStatusCode enum value
451	                # Fall back to value format (e.g., "OK", "ERROR")
452	                status_code = SpanStatusCode(status_code_str)
453	            status = SpanStatus(
454	                status_code=status_code,
455	                description=data["status"].get("message", ""),
456	            )
457	
458	            end_time_ns = data.get("end_time_unix_nano")
459	            end_time_ns = int(end_time_ns) if end_time_ns else None
460	
461	            otel_span = OTelReadableSpan(
462	                name=data["name"],
463	                context=build_otel_context(otel_trace_id, span_id),
464	                parent=build_otel_context(otel_trace_id, parent_id) if parent_id else None,
465	                start_time=int(data["start_time_unix_nano"]),
466	                end_time=end_time_ns,
467	                attributes=data["attributes"],
468	                status=status.to_otel_status(),
469	                # Setting an empty resource explicitly. Otherwise OTel create a new Resource by
470	                # Resource.create(), which introduces a significant overhead in some environments.
471	                # https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/15625
472	                resource=_OTelResource.get_empty(),
473	                events=[
474	                    OTelEvent(
475	                        name=event["name"],
476	                        timestamp=int(event["time_unix_nano"]),
477	                        attributes=event.get("attributes", {}),
478	                    )
479	                    for event in data.get("events", [])
480	                ],
481	            )
482	            span = cls(otel_span)
483	
484	            # Deserialize links if present
485	            if links_data := data.get("links"):
486	                span._links = [Link.from_dict(link_dict) for link_dict in links_data]
487	
488	            return span
489	        except Exception as e:
490	            raise MlflowException(
491	                "Failed to create a Span object from the given dictionary",
492	                INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
493	            ) from e

533	    @classmethod
534	    def from_otel_proto(
535	        cls,
536	        otel_proto_span: OTelProtoSpan,
537	        location_id: str | None = None,
538	        *,
539	        preserve_request_id: bool = False,
540	        resource: OTelProtoResource | None = None,
541	    ) -> "Span":
542	        """
543	        Create a Span from an OpenTelemetry protobuf span.
544	
545	        This is an internal method used for receiving spans via OTel protocol. By default,
546	        MLflow derives the canonical ``mlflow.traceRequestId`` from the OTLP trace ID so server
547	        ingest does not trust a client-sent request ID. Set ``preserve_request_id=True`` only for
548	        trusted internal round-trip flows, such as archived trace payload deserialization, where
549	        the stored MLflow request ID must be preserved exactly if present.
550	        """
551	        # Validate required fields - empty bytes indicate missing trace_id or span_id
552	        if not otel_proto_span.trace_id:
553	            raise ValueError("trace_id is required but was empty")
554	        if not otel_proto_span.span_id:
555	            raise ValueError("span_id is required but was empty")
556	
557	        trace_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.trace_id)
558	        span_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.span_id)
559	        parent_id = None
560	        if otel_proto_span.parent_span_id:
561	            parent_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.parent_span_id)
562	
563	        # Convert OTel proto status code directly to OTel SDK status
564	        if otel_proto_span.status.code == OTelProtoStatus.STATUS_CODE_OK:
565	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.OK
566	        elif otel_proto_span.status.code == OTelProtoStatus.STATUS_CODE_ERROR:
567	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.ERROR
568	        else:
569	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.UNSET
570	
571	        serialized_attributes = {
572	            attr.key: dump_span_attribute_value(_decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value))
573	            for attr in otel_proto_span.attributes
574	        }
575	        mlflow_trace_id = (
576	            generate_trace_id_v4_from_otel_trace_id(trace_id, location_id)
577	            if location_id
578	            else generate_mlflow_trace_id_from_otel_trace_id(trace_id)
579	        )
580	        serialized_request_id = dump_span_attribute_value(mlflow_trace_id)
581	        if preserve_request_id:
582	            serialized_request_id = serialized_attributes.get(
583	                SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID, serialized_request_id
584	            )
585	        request_id = json.loads(serialized_request_id)
586	
587	        # Convert proto Resource to OTel SDK Resource if provided.
588	        # We avoid _OTelResource.create() which has significant overhead from
589	        # environment variable reads (see https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/15625).
590	        if resource is not None and resource.attributes:
591	            resource_attrs = {
592	                attr.key: _decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value) for attr in resource.attributes
593	            }
594	            otel_resource = _OTelResource(resource_attrs)
595	        else:
596	            otel_resource = _OTelResource.get_empty()
597	
598	        links = [Link.from_otel_proto(proto_link) for proto_link in otel_proto_span.links]
599	        for link in links:
600	            link.trace_id = _normalize_link_trace_id(link.trace_id, request_id)
601	
602	        otel_span = OTelReadableSpan(
603	            name=otel_proto_span.name,
604	            context=build_otel_context(trace_id, span_id),
605	            parent=build_otel_context(trace_id, parent_id) if parent_id else None,
606	            start_time=otel_proto_span.start_time_unix_nano,
607	            end_time=otel_proto_span.end_time_unix_nano,
608	            # we need to dump the attribute value to be consistent with span.set_attribute behavior
609	            attributes={
610	                **serialized_attributes,
611	                SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID: serialized_request_id,
612	            },
613	            status=OTelStatus(status_code, otel_proto_span.status.message or None),
614	            events=[
615	                OTelEvent(
616	                    name=event.name,
617	                    timestamp=event.time_unix_nano,
618	                    attributes={
619	                        attr.key: _decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value)
620	                        for attr in event.attributes
621	                    },
622	                )
623	                for event in otel_proto_span.events
624	            ],
625	            resource=otel_resource,
626	        )
627	
628	        span = cls(otel_span)
629	        span._links = links
630	        return span
631	
632	    def to_otel_proto(self) -> OTelProtoSpan:
633	        """
634	        Convert to OpenTelemetry protobuf span format for OTLP export.
635	        This is an internal method used by the REST store for logging spans.
636	
637	        Returns:
638	            An OpenTelemetry protobuf Span message.
639	        """
640	        otel_span = OTelProtoSpan()
641	        otel_span.trace_id = bytes.fromhex(self._trace_id)
642	        otel_span.span_id = bytes.fromhex(self.span_id)
643	
644	        otel_span.name = self.name
645	        otel_span.start_time_unix_nano = self.start_time_ns
646	        if self.end_time_ns:
647	            otel_span.end_time_unix_nano = self.end_time_ns
648	
649	        if self.parent_id:
650	            otel_span.parent_span_id = bytes.fromhex(self.parent_id)
651	
652	        otel_span.status.CopyFrom(self.status.to_otel_proto_status())
653	
654	        for key, value in self.attributes.items():
655	            attr = otel_span.attributes.add()
656	            attr.key = key
657	            _set_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value, value)
658	
659	        for event in self.events:
660	            otel_event = event.to_otel_proto()
661	            otel_span.events.append(otel_event)
662	
663	        # Convert links to OTLP proto format
664	        for link in self.links:
665	            proto_link = otel_span.links.add()
666	            # Convert MLflow trace ID (tr-xxx or trace:/loc/xxx) back to OTel bytes
667	            link_trace_id_hex = parse_trace_id_v4(link.trace_id)[1].removeprefix(
668	                TRACE_REQUEST_ID_PREFIX
669	            )
670	            proto_link.trace_id = decode_id(link_trace_id_hex).to_bytes(16, "big")
671	            proto_link.span_id = decode_id(link.span_id).to_bytes(8, "big")
672	
673	            # Add link attributes
674	            if link.attributes:
675	                for key, value in link.attributes.items():
676	                    attr = proto_link.attributes.add()
677	                    attr.key = key
678	                    _set_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value, value)
679	
680	        return otel_span
681

683	def _encode_span_id_to_byte(span_id: int | None) -> bytes:

685	    return span_id.to_bytes(length=8, byteorder="big", signed=False)

699	    bytes = base64.b64decode(trace_or_span_id_b64)
700	    return int.from_bytes(bytes, byteorder="big", signed=False)

706	        return True

708	        return False

711	class LiveSpan(Span):
712	    """
713	    A "live" version of the :py:class:`Span <mlflow.entities.Span>` class.
714	
715	    The live spans are those being created and updated during the application runtime.
716	    When users start a new span using the tracing APIs within their code, this live span
717	    object is returned to get and set the span attributes, status, events, and etc.
718	    """
719	
720	    def __init__(
721	        self,
722	        otel_span: OTelSpan,
723	        trace_id: str,
724	        span_type: str = SpanType.UNKNOWN,
725	    ):
726	        """
727	        The `otel_span` argument takes an instance of OpenTelemetry Span class, which is
728	        indeed a subclass of ReadableSpan. Thanks to this, the getter methods of the Span
729	        class can be reused without any modification.
730	
731	        Note that the constructor doesn't call the super().__init__ method, because the Span
732	        initialization logic is a bit different from the immutable span.
733	        """
734	        if not isinstance(otel_span, OTelReadableSpan):
735	            raise MlflowException(
736	                "The `otel_span` argument for the LiveSpan class must be an instance of "
737	                f"trace.Span, but got {type(otel_span)}.",
738	                INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
739	            )
740	
741	        self._span = otel_span
742	        self._attachments: dict[str, Attachment] = {}
743	        self._attributes = _SpanAttributesRegistry(otel_span)
744	        self._attributes.set(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID, trace_id)
745	        self._attributes.set(SpanAttributeKey.SPAN_TYPE, span_type)
746	        otel_links = getattr(otel_span, "links", ())
747	        self._links: list["Link"] = [
748	            _link_from_otel_link(otel_link, trace_id) for otel_link in otel_links
749	        ]
750	        # Track the original span name for deduplication purposes during span logging.
751	        # Why: When traces contain multiple spans with identical names (e.g., multiple "LLM"
752	        # or "query" spans), it's difficult for users to distinguish between them in the UI
753	        # and logs. As spans are logged, we incrementally add numeric suffixes (_1, _2, etc.) to
754	        # make each span uniquely identifiable within its trace
755	        self._original_name = otel_span.name
756	
757	    def set_span_type(self, span_type: str):
758	        """Set the type of the span."""
759	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.SPAN_TYPE, span_type)
760	
761	    def set_description(self, description: str):
762	        """Set the description of the span."""
763	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.DESCRIPTION, description)
764	
765	    def set_log_level(self, level: SpanLogLevel | str):
766	        """
767	        Set the severity level of the span.
768	
769	        Args:
770	            level: A :py:class:`SpanLogLevel <mlflow.entities.SpanLogLevel>` or
771	                its name (e.g. ``"INFO"``).
772	        """
773	        normalized = SpanLogLevel.from_value(level)
774	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.LOG_LEVEL, int(normalized))
775	
776	    def _is_recording(self) -> bool:
777	        return self._span.is_recording()
778	
779	    def set_inputs(self, inputs: Any):
780	        """Set the input values to the span."""
781	        extract_base64 = self._should_extract_base64()
782	        inputs = self._extract_attachments(inputs, extract_base64)
783	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.INPUTS, inputs)
784	        # Second pass on the serialized form handles framework objects
785	        # (e.g., Pydantic models, LangChain BaseMessage) that only become
786	        # plain dicts after JSON serialization by set_attribute.
787	        if extract_base64:
788	            self._extract_attachments_from_serialized(SpanAttributeKey.INPUTS)
789	
790	    def set_outputs(self, outputs: Any):
791	        """Set the output values to the span."""
792	        extract_base64 = self._should_extract_base64()
793	        outputs = self._extract_attachments(outputs, extract_base64)
794	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.OUTPUTS, outputs)
795	        if extract_base64:
796	            self._extract_attachments_from_serialized(SpanAttributeKey.OUTPUTS)
797	
798	    def _extract_attachments_from_serialized(self, attr_key: str):
799	        """Re-extract attachments from the serialized attribute value.
800	
801	        Handles cases where the first extraction pass couldn't recurse into
802	        framework-specific objects (e.g., LangChain BaseMessage) that only
803	        become plain dicts after JSON serialization.
804	        """
805	        serialized = self._attributes.get(attr_key)
806	        if serialized is None:
807	            return
808	        attachments_before = len(self._attachments)
809	        extracted = self._extract_attachments(serialized, extract_base64=True)
810	        if len(self._attachments) > attachments_before:
811	            self.set_attribute(attr_key, extracted)
812	
813	    def _extract_attachments(self, value: Any, extract_base64: bool) -> Any:
814	        if isinstance(value, Attachment):
815	            return self._store_attachment(value)
816	        if extract_base64:
817	            if isinstance(value, str):
818	                converted = self._try_convert_data_uri(value)
819	                if converted is not None:
820	                    return converted
821	            if isinstance(value, dict):
822	                converted = self._try_convert_structured_content(value)
823	                if converted is not None:
824	                    # Recurse into the converted dict to catch remaining patterns
825	                    # in sibling keys (e.g. a data URI in another field)
826	                    if isinstance(converted, dict):
827	                        return {
828	                            k: self._extract_attachments(v, extract_base64)
829	                            for k, v in converted.items()
830	                        }
831	                    return converted
832	        if isinstance(value, dict):
833	            return {k: self._extract_attachments(v, extract_base64) for k, v in value.items()}
834	        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
835	            return [self._extract_attachments(item, extract_base64) for item in value]
836	        return value
837	
838	    def _store_attachment(self, attachment: Attachment) -> str:
839	        from mlflow.environment_variables import MLFLOW_TRACE_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE
840	
841	        if not self._is_recording():
842	            _logger.debug("Skipping attachment storage because the span is no longer recording.")
843	            return attachment.ref(self.trace_id)
844	
845	        max_size = MLFLOW_TRACE_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE.get()
846	        if max_size is not None and max_size > 0 and len(attachment.content_bytes) > max_size:
847	            size_bytes = len(attachment.content_bytes)
848	            msg = (
849	                f"Attachment too large ({size_bytes} bytes > {max_size} bytes limit). "
850	                f"Content discarded."
851	            )
852	            _logger.warning(msg)
853	            self.record_exception(msg)
854	            return f"[Attachment too large: {size_bytes} bytes exceeds {max_size} bytes limit]"
855	        ref = attachment.ref(self.trace_id)
856	        self._attachments[attachment.id] = attachment
857	        return ref
858	
859	    @staticmethod
860	    def _should_extract_base64() -> bool:
861	        from mlflow.environment_variables import MLFLOW_TRACE_EXTRACT_ATTACHMENTS
862	
863	        return MLFLOW_TRACE_EXTRACT_ATTACHMENTS.get()
864	
865	    def _try_convert_data_uri(self, value: str) -> str | None:
866	        if not value.startswith("data:") or ";base64," not in value:
867	            return None

1305	    def from_immutable_span(
1306	        cls,
1307	        span: Span,
1308	        parent_span_id: str | None = None,
1309	        trace_id: str | None = None,
1310	        experiment_id: str | None = None,
1311	        otel_trace_id: str | None = None,
1312	    ) -> "LiveSpan":
1313	        """
1314	        Create a new LiveSpan object from the given immutable span by
1315	        cloning the underlying OpenTelemetry span within current context.
1316	
1317	        This is particularly useful when we merging a remote trace into the current trace.
1318	        We cannot merge the remote trace directly, because it is already stored as an immutable
1319	        span, meaning that we cannot update metadata like trace ID, parent span ID,
1320	        which are necessary for merging the trace.
1321	
1322	        Args:
1323	            span: The immutable span object to clone.
1324	            parent_span_id: The parent span ID of the new span.
1325	                If it is None, the span will be created as a root span.
1326	            trace_id: The trace ID to be set on the new span. Specify this if you want to
1327	                create the new span with a particular trace ID.
1328	            experiment_id: The experiment ID to be set on the new span. If not specified, the
1329	                experiment ID will be set to the current experiment ID.
1330	            otel_trace_id: The OpenTelemetry trace ID of the new span in hex encoded format.
1331	                If not specified, the newly generated trace ID will be used.
1332	
1333	        Returns:
1334	            The new LiveSpan object with the same state as the original span.
1335	
1336	        :meta private:
1337	        """
1338	        from mlflow.tracing.trace_manager import InMemoryTraceManager
1339	
1340	        trace_manager = InMemoryTraceManager.get_instance()
1341	        parent_span = trace_manager.get_span_from_id(trace_id, parent_span_id)
1342	
1343	        # Create a new span with the same name, parent, and start time
1344	        otel_span = mlflow.tracing.provider.start_detached_span(
1345	            name=span.name,
1346	            parent=parent_span._span if parent_span else None,
1347	            start_time_ns=span.start_time_ns,
1348	            experiment_id=experiment_id,
1349	        )
1350	
1351	        # The latter one from attributes is the newly generated trace ID by the span processor.
1352	        trace_id = trace_id or json.loads(otel_span.attributes.get(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID))
1353	        # Span processor registers a new span in the in-memory trace manager, but we want to pop it
1354	        clone_span = trace_manager._traces[trace_id].span_dict.pop(
1355	            encode_span_id(otel_span.context.span_id)
1356	        )
1357	
1358	        # Copy all the attributes, inputs, outputs, and events from the original span
1359	        clone_span.set_status(span.status)
1360	        clone_span.set_attributes({
1361	            k: v for k, v in span.attributes.items() if k != SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID
1362	        })
1363	        if span.inputs:
1364	            clone_span.set_inputs(span.inputs)
1365	        if span.outputs:
1366	            clone_span.set_outputs(span.outputs)
1367	        for event in span.events:
1368	            clone_span.add_event(event)
1369	        if span.links:
1370	            _logger.warning(
1371	                "Span links on span '%s' will not be retained when copying to a new trace "
1372	                "because link trace IDs may not resolve in the destination trace context.",
1373	                span.name,
1374	            )
1375	
1376	        # Update trace ID and span ID
1377	        context = span._span.get_span_context()
1378	        clone_span._span._context = SpanContext(
1379	            # Override otel_trace_id if provided, otherwise use the new trace ID
1380	            trace_id=decode_id(otel_trace_id) if otel_trace_id else otel_span.context.trace_id,
1381	            # Re-use same span ID as their ID space is local to the trace
1382	            span_id=context.span_id,
1383	            is_remote=context.is_remote,
1384	            # Override trace flag as if it is sampled within current context.
1385	            trace_flags=TraceFlags(TraceFlags.SAMPLED),
1386	        )
1387	
1388	        return clone_span

1405	    payload, artifact responses can emit that string directly and skip
1406	    ``json.dumps``.
1407	    """
1408	
1409	    def __init__(self, span_dict: dict[str, Any], *, raw_json: str | None = None):
1410	        # Skip Span.__init__: we intentionally avoid constructing an OTel span
1411	        # until a caller needs property access or OTLP conversion.
1412	        self.__dict__["_span_dict"] = span_dict
1413	        self.__dict__["_raw_json"] = raw_json
1414	        self.__dict__["_materialized"] = False
1415	
1416	    @classmethod
1417	    def from_stored_content(cls, content: str) -> "LazySpan":
1418	        """Build a ``LazySpan`` from a TRACKING_STORE ``spans.content`` value."""
1419	        # Deferred to avoid a circular import with mlflow.tracing.otel.translation.
1420	        from mlflow.tracing.otel.translation import translate_loaded_span_with_status
1421	
1422	        span_dict = json.loads(content)
1423	        modified = translate_loaded_span_with_status(span_dict)
1424	        return cls(span_dict, raw_json=None if modified else content)
1425	
1426	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1427	        # to_dict() returns the live mutable dict. Once a caller can mutate it,
1428	        # raw JSON passthrough is no longer safe for subsequent exports.
1429	        self.__dict__["_raw_json"] = None
1430	        return self.__dict__["_span_dict"]
1431	
1432	    def json_for_export(self) -> str:
1433	        """Return JSON text for artifact export without an unnecessary re-dump."""
1434	        raw_json = self.__dict__["_raw_json"]
1435	        if raw_json is not None:
1436	            return raw_json
1437	        return json.dumps(self.__dict__["_span_dict"], separators=(",", ":"))
1438	
1439	    def _ensure_materialized(self) -> None:
1440	        if self.__dict__["_materialized"]:
1441	            return
1442	        span = Span.from_dict(self.__dict__["_span_dict"])
1443	        self.__dict__["_span"] = span._span
1444	        self.__dict__["_attributes"] = span._attributes
1445	        # Attachments restored by `__setstate__` are kept.
1446	        self.__dict__.setdefault("_attachments", span._attachments)
1447	        self.__dict__["_links"] = span._links
1448	        self.__dict__["_materialized"] = True
1449	
1450	    def __getstate__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1451	        # Carry either the raw JSON or the dict, never both, and keep the restored span lazy.
1452	        raw_json = self.__dict__["_raw_json"]
1453	        if raw_json is not None:
1454	            state = {"raw_json": raw_json}
1455	        else:
1456	            state = {"span_dict": self.__dict__["_span_dict"]}
1457	        if attachments := self.__dict__.get("_attachments"):
1458	            state["attachments"] = dict(attachments)
1459	        return state
1460	
1461	    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
1462	        raw_json = state.get("raw_json")
1463	        span_dict = json.loads(raw_json) if raw_json is not None else state["span_dict"]
1464	        LazySpan.__init__(self, span_dict, raw_json=raw_json)
1465	        if attachments := state.get("attachments"):
1466	            self.__dict__["_attachments"] = dict(attachments)
1467	
1468	    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
1469	        # Copy/pickle probe dunder hooks on instances whose `__dict__` is not populated yet,
1470	        # so those lookups must not trigger materialization.
1471	        if (name.startswith("__") and name.endswith("__")) or "_span_dict" not in self.__dict__:
1472	            raise AttributeError(f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'")
1473	        self._ensure_materialized()
1474	        try:
1475	            return object.__getattribute__(self, name)
1476	        except AttributeError:
1477	            return super().__getattr__(name)
1478	
1479	    def __repr__(self):
1480	        if self.__dict__.get("_materialized"):
1481	            return super().__repr__()
1482	        span_dict = self.__dict__["_span_dict"]
1483	        name = span_dict.get("name")
1484	        attributes = span_dict.get("attributes") or {}
1485	        request_id = attributes.get(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID)
1486	        # request_id may still be JSON-encoded in persisted attributes.
1487	        if isinstance(request_id, str):
1488	            try:
1489	                request_id = json.loads(request_id)
1490	            except (TypeError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
1491	                pass
1492	        return (
1493	            f"LazySpan(name={name!r}, trace_id={request_id!r}, "
1494	            f"span_id={span_dict.get('span_id')!r}, "
1495	            f"parent_id={span_dict.get('parent_span_id')!r})"

1610	class _SpanAttributesRegistry:
1611	    """
1612	    A utility class to manage the span attributes.
1613	
1614	    In MLflow users can add arbitrary key-value pairs to the span attributes, however,
1615	    OpenTelemetry only allows a limited set of types to be stored in the attribute values.
1616	    Therefore, we serialize all values into JSON string before storing them in the span.
1617	    This class provides simple getter and setter methods to interact with the span attributes
1618	    without worrying about the serde process.
1619	    """
1620	
1621	    def __init__(self, otel_span: OTelSpan):
1622	        self._span = otel_span
1623	
1624	    def get_all(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1625	        return {key: self.get(key) for key in self._span.attributes.keys()}
1626	
1627	    def get(self, key: str):
1628	        if serialized_value := self._span.attributes.get(key):
1629	            try:
1630	                return json.loads(serialized_value)
1631	            except Exception:
1632	                # If failed to deserialize (e.g., string value is directly set to OTel span),
1633	                # return the original value as is.
1634	                return serialized_value
1635	
1636	    def set(self, key: str, value: Any):
1637	        if not isinstance(key, str):
1638	            _logger.warning(f"Attribute key must be a string, but got {type(key)}. Skipping.")
1639	            return
1640	
1641	        # NB: OpenTelemetry attribute can store not only string but also a few primitives like
1642	        #   int, float, bool, and list of them. However, we serialize all into JSON string here
1643	        #   for the simplicity in deserialization process.
1644	        self._span.set_attribute(key, dump_span_attribute_value(value))
1645

1647	class _CachedSpanAttributesRegistry(_SpanAttributesRegistry):
1648	    """
1649	    A cache-enabled version of the SpanAttributesRegistry.
1650	
1651	    The caching helps to avoid the redundant deserialization of the attribute, however, it does
1652	    not handle the value change well. Therefore, this class should only be used for the persisted
1653	    spans that are immutable, and thus implemented as a subclass of _SpanAttributesRegistry.
1654	    """
1655	
1656	    def __init__(self, otel_span: OTelSpan):
1657	        super().__init__(otel_span)
1658	        self._cache: dict[str, Any] = {}
1659	
1660	    def get(self, key: str):
1661	        if key not in self._cache:
1662	            self._cache[key] = super().get(key)
1663	        return self._cache[key]
1664	
1665	    def set(self, key: str, value: Any):
1666	        raise MlflowException(
1667	            "The attributes of the immutable span must not be updated.", INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
1668	        )

616	    it JSON-encodes mlflow.traceRequestId into the live OTel span via LiveSpan.__init__.
617	    The OTLP proto then carries the already-encoded value (e.g. '"tr-abc"' with inner quotes).
618	    from_otel_proto() must not double-encode it — the server-computed ID must always win.

629	    # _SpanAttributesRegistry.set() calls dump_span_attribute_value("tr-abc") = '"tr-abc"'
630	    # so the OTel span attribute stored in memory is the JSON-encoded string '"tr-abc"'.

45	def capture_function_input_args(func, args, kwargs) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
46	    try:
47	        func_signature = inspect.signature(func)
48	        bound_arguments = func_signature.bind(*args, **kwargs)
49	        bound_arguments.apply_defaults()
50	
51	        # Remove `self` from bound arguments if it exists
52	        if bound_arguments.arguments.get("self"):
53	            del bound_arguments.arguments["self"]
54	
55	        # Remove `cls` from bound arguments if it's the first parameter and it's a type
56	        # This detects classmethods more reliably
57	        params = list(bound_arguments.arguments.keys())
58	        if params and params[0] == "cls" and isinstance(bound_arguments.arguments["cls"], type):
59	            del bound_arguments.arguments["cls"]
60	
61	        return bound_arguments.arguments
62	    except Exception:
63	        _logger.warning(f"Failed to capture inputs for function {func.__name__}.")
64	        return None

67	class TraceJSONEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
68	    """
69	    Custom JSON encoder for serializing non-OpenTelemetry compatible objects in a trace or span.
70	
71	    Trace may contain types that require custom serialization logic, such as Pydantic models,
72	    non-JSON-serializable types, etc.
73	    """
74	
75	    def default(self, obj):
76	        if isinstance(obj, pydantic.BaseModel):
77	            return obj.model_dump()
78	
79	        # Some dataclass object defines __str__ method that doesn't return the full object
80	        # representation, so we use dict representation instead.
81	        # E.g. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/29ece9b058f6b9a1cf29bc723ed4aa3a39879ad5/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/chat_engine/types.py#L63-L64
82	        if is_dataclass(obj):
83	            # Use shallow field extraction instead of asdict() to avoid copy.deepcopy(),
84	            # which can leave partially-constructed objects (e.g. AsyncHttpxClientWrapper
85	            # missing _state) that crash during garbage collection.
86	            # json.dumps will recursively call default() on nested values, so we still
87	            # get full recursive serialization without the deepcopy hazard.
88	            try:
89	                return {f.name: getattr(obj, f.name) for f in fields(obj)}
90	            except Exception:
91	                pass
92	
93	        # Some object has dangerous side effect in __str__ method, so we use class name instead.
94	        if not self._is_safe_to_encode_str(obj):
95	            return type(obj)
96	
97	        try:
98	            return super().default(obj)
99	        except TypeError:
100	            return str(obj)
101	
102	    def _is_safe_to_encode_str(self, obj) -> bool:
103	        """Check if it's safe to encode the object as a string."""
104	        try:
105	            # These Llama Index objects are not safe to encode as string, because their __str__
106	            # method consumes the stream and make it unusable.
107	            # E.g. https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/54f2da61ba8a573284ab8336f2b2810d948c3877/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/base/response/schema.py#L120-L127

205	class SpanAggregationNode:
206	    """Minimal view of a span used for tree-aware aggregation of usage/cost data.
207	
208	    Allows sharing the aggregation logic between in-memory spans (client) and
209	    spans deserialized from a tracking store (server).
210	    """
211	
212	    span_id: str
213	    parent_id: str | None
214	    data: dict[str, Any] | None
215	
216	
217	def _aggregate_from_nodes(
218	    nodes: list[SpanAggregationNode],
219	    keys: list[str],
220	    default: int | float,
221	    optional_keys: list[str] | None = None,
222	) -> dict[str, int | float] | None:
223	    """Generic aggregation of data from span nodes using DFS traversal.
224	
225	    Avoids double-counting by skipping nodes whose ancestors already have the data.
226	
227	    Trace-level usage (``CHAT_USAGE``) and cost (``LLM_COST``) are produced by two
228	    *independent* calls to this function, each deduping on its own attribute. They
229	    reconcile for the common leaf-only integrations (direct providers, langchain,
230	    llama_index, crewai, autogen, ag2), where usage sits on the same priced LLM spans as
231	    cost so both boundaries coincide. They can differ only when a span carries usage but
232	    no cost -- a rollup-on-parent integration (e.g. pydantic_ai, dspy, agno) that sets
233	    cumulative usage on an unpriced agent/module span; even then a faithful rollup (parent
234	    usage == sum of priced leaves) still reconciles. A cache-heavy trace whose cost looks
235	    large relative to ``total_tokens`` is a separate token-accounting gap (``total_tokens``
236	    excludes cache tokens that cost is priced on), not this aggregation.
237	
238	    Args:
239	        nodes: List of span nodes to aggregate from.
240	        keys: Keys to aggregate. Always included in the result.
241	        default: Default value (0 for int, 0.0 for float) that also determines return type.
242	        optional_keys: Additional keys to aggregate. Only included in the result
243	            when the key is present in the node data.
244	
245	    Returns:
246	        Aggregated dictionary with the keys, or None if no data found.
247	    """
248	    totals: dict[str, int | float] = dict.fromkeys(keys, default)
249	    has_data = False
250	
251	    node_ids = {node.span_id for node in nodes}
252	    children_map: defaultdict[str, list[SpanAggregationNode]] = defaultdict(list)
253	    roots: list[SpanAggregationNode] = []
254	
255	    for node in nodes:
256	        parent_id = node.parent_id
257	        if parent_id and parent_id in node_ids:
258	            children_map[parent_id].append(node)
259	        else:
260	            roots.append(node)
261	
262	    # Iterative DFS with an explicit stack, instead of recursion, to avoid overflowing
263	    # Python's call stack for deeply nested traces (~1000+ levels). A recursive walk here
264	    # used to abort root-span finalization and permanently corrupt the trace.
265	    #
266	    # Visit order is irrelevant: totals is a sum and has_data an OR (both commutative), and
267	    # each node's ancestor_has_data is fixed by its ancestor chain, not by sibling visit
268	    # order. So a plain stack (no reversed()) yields identical results.
269	    stack: list[tuple[SpanAggregationNode, bool]] = [(root, False) for root in roots]
270	    while stack:
271	        node, ancestor_has_data = stack.pop()
272	
273	        data = node.data
274	        node_has_data = data is not None
275	
276	        if node_has_data and not ancestor_has_data:
277	            for k in keys:
278	                totals[k] += data.get(k, default)
279	            for k in optional_keys or []:
280	                if k in data:
281	                    totals[k] = totals.get(k, default) + data[k]
282	            has_data = True
283	
284	        next_ancestor_has_data = ancestor_has_data or node_has_data
285	        stack.extend(
286	            (child, next_ancestor_has_data) for child in children_map.get(node.span_id, [])
287	        )
288	
289	    if not has_data:
290	        return None
291	
292	    return totals

373	    if not model_provider and model_name.startswith(("databricks-", "databricks/")):
374	        model_provider = "databricks"
375	
376	    prompt_tokens = usage.get(TokenUsageKey.INPUT_TOKENS, 0)
377	    completion_tokens = usage.get(TokenUsageKey.OUTPUT_TOKENS, 0)
378	
379	    if prompt_tokens == 0 and completion_tokens == 0:
380	        return None
381	
382	    cache_kwargs = {}
383	    if (cached := usage.get(TokenUsageKey.CACHE_READ_INPUT_TOKENS)) is not None:
384	        cache_kwargs["cache_read_input_tokens"] = cached
385	    if (created := usage.get(TokenUsageKey.CACHE_CREATION_INPUT_TOKENS)) is not None:
386	        cache_kwargs["cache_creation_input_tokens"] = created
387	
388	    try:
389	        import litellm
390	        from litellm import cost_per_token
391	    except ImportError:
392	        from mlflow.utils.providers import cost_per_token
393	
394	        litellm = None
395	
396	    # The 1-hour cache-creation breakdown is only understood by MLflow's builtin cost_per_token;
397	    # litellm's signature does not accept it, so only pass it when falling back to the builtin.
398	    if (
399	        litellm is None
400	        and (above_1hr := usage.get(TokenUsageKey.CACHE_CREATION_INPUT_TOKENS_ABOVE_1HR))
401	        is not None
402	    ):
403	        cache_kwargs["cache_creation_input_tokens_above_1hr"] = above_1hr
404	
405	    if litellm is not None:
406	        original_suppress = getattr(litellm, "suppress_debug_info")
407	
408	    try:
409	        if litellm is not None:
410	            # Suppress litellm debug messages (e.g. "Provider List: ...") unless
411	            # MLflow's logger is set to DEBUG level.
412	            litellm.suppress_debug_info = not _logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)
413	
414	        # When provider is known, try it first — this is a fast single-provider lookup
415	        # and avoids the slower all-provider scan.
416	        result = None
417	        if model_provider:
418	            try:
419	                result = cost_per_token(
420	                    model=model_name,
421	                    prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
422	                    completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
423	                    custom_llm_provider=model_provider.lower(),
424	                    **cache_kwargs,
425	                )
426	            except Exception:
427	                pass
428	
429	        # Fallback: try without provider (for litellm this may match by model name alone,
430	        # for builtin this scans bundled providers).
431	        if result is None:
432	            try:
433	                result = cost_per_token(
434	                    model=model_name,
435	                    prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
436	                    completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
437	                    **cache_kwargs,
438	                )
439	            except Exception:
440	                pass
441	    finally:
442	        if litellm is not None:
443	            litellm.suppress_debug_info = original_suppress
444	
445	    if result is None:
446	        _logger.debug(f"Failed to calculate cost for model {model_name}")
447	        return None
448	
449	    input_cost_usd, output_cost_usd = result
450	    return {
451	        CostKey.INPUT_COST: input_cost_usd,
452	        CostKey.OUTPUT_COST: output_cost_usd,
453	        CostKey.TOTAL_COST: input_cost_usd + output_cost_usd,
454	    }

706	def _calculate_percentile(sorted_data: list[float], percentile: float) -> float:
707	    """
708	    Calculate the percentile value from sorted data.
709	
710	    Args:
711	        sorted_data: A sorted list of numeric values
712	        percentile: The percentile to calculate (e.g., 0.25 for 25th percentile)
713	
714	    Returns:
715	        The percentile value
716	    """
717	    if not sorted_data:
718	        return 0.0
719	
720	    n = len(sorted_data)
721	    index = percentile * (n - 1)
722	    lower = int(index)
723	    upper = lower + 1
724	
725	    if upper >= n:
726	        return sorted_data[-1]
727	
728	    # Linear interpolation between two nearest values
729	    weight = index - lower
730	    return sorted_data[lower] * (1 - weight) + sorted_data[upper] * weight

733	def add_size_stats_to_trace_metadata(trace: Trace):
734	    """
735	    Calculate the stats of trace and span sizes and add it as a metadata to the trace.
736	
737	    This method modifies the trace object in place by adding a new tag.
738	
739	    Note: For simplicity, we calculate the size without considering the size metadata itself.
740	    This provides a close approximation without requiring complex calculations.
741	
742	    This function must not throw an exception.
743	    """
744	    from mlflow.entities import Trace, TraceData
745	
746	    try:
747	        span_sizes = []
748	        for span in trace.data.spans:
749	            span_json = json.dumps(span.to_dict(), cls=TraceJSONEncoder)
750	            span_sizes.append(len(span_json.encode("utf-8")))
751	
752	        # NB: To compute the size of the total trace, we need to include the size of the
753	        # the trace info and the parent dicts for the spans. To avoid serializing spans
754	        # again (which can be expensive), we compute the size of the trace without spans
755	        # and combine it with the total size of the spans.
756	        empty_trace = Trace(info=trace.info, data=TraceData(spans=[]))
757	        metadata_size = len((empty_trace.to_json()).encode("utf-8"))
758	
759	        # NB: the third term is the size of comma separators between spans (", ").
760	        trace_size_bytes = sum(span_sizes) + metadata_size + (len(span_sizes) - 1) * 2
761	
762	        # Sort span sizes for percentile calculation
763	        sorted_span_sizes = sorted(span_sizes)
764	
765	        size_stats = {
766	            TraceSizeStatsKey.TOTAL_SIZE_BYTES: trace_size_bytes,
767	            TraceSizeStatsKey.NUM_SPANS: len(span_sizes),
768	            TraceSizeStatsKey.MAX_SPAN_SIZE_BYTES: max(span_sizes),
769	            TraceSizeStatsKey.P25_SPAN_SIZE_BYTES: int(
770	                _calculate_percentile(sorted_span_sizes, 0.25)
771	            ),
772	            TraceSizeStatsKey.P50_SPAN_SIZE_BYTES: int(
773	                _calculate_percentile(sorted_span_sizes, 0.50)
774	            ),
775	            TraceSizeStatsKey.P75_SPAN_SIZE_BYTES: int(
776	                _calculate_percentile(sorted_span_sizes, 0.75)
777	            ),
778	        }
779	
780	        trace.info.trace_metadata[TraceMetadataKey.SIZE_STATS] = json.dumps(size_stats)
781	        # Keep the total size as a separate metadata for backward compatibility
782	        trace.info.trace_metadata[TraceMetadataKey.SIZE_BYTES] = str(trace_size_bytes)
783	    except Exception:
784	        _logger.warning("Failed to add size stats to trace metadata.", exc_info=True)
785

787	def update_trace_state_from_span_conditionally(trace, root_span):
788	    """
789	    Update trace state from span status, but only if the user hasn't explicitly set
790	    a different trace status.
791	
792	    This utility preserves user-set trace status while maintaining default behavior
793	    for traces that haven't been explicitly configured. Used by trace processors when
794	    converting traces to an exportable state.
795	
796	    Args:
797	        trace: The trace object to potentially update
798	        root_span: The root span whose status may be used to update the trace state
799	    """
800	    from mlflow.entities.trace_state import TraceState
801	
802	    # Only update trace state from span status if trace is still IN_PROGRESS
803	    # If the trace state is anything else, it means the user explicitly set it
804	    # and we should preserve it
805	    if trace.info.state == TraceState.IN_PROGRESS:
806	        state = TraceState.from_otel_status(root_span.status)
807	        # If the root span is created by the native OpenTelemetry SDK, the status code can be UNSET
808	        # (default value when an otel span is ended). Override it to OK here to avoid backend error.
809	        if state == TraceState.STATE_UNSPECIFIED:
810	            state = TraceState.OK
811	        trace.info.state = state

871	@contextmanager
872	def _bypass_attribute_guard(span: OTelSpan) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
873	    """
874	    OpenTelemetry does not allow setting attributes if the span has end time defined.
875	    https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/blob/d327927d0274a320466feec6fba6d6ddb287dc5a/opentelemetry-sdk/src/opentelemetry/sdk/trace/__init__.py#L849-L851
876	
877	    However, we need to set some attributes within `on_end` handler of the span processor,
878	    where the span is already marked as ended. This context manager is a hacky workaround
879	    to bypass the attribute guard.
880	
881	    Since opentelemetry-sdk 1.43.0, `Span.end()` additionally marks the span's
882	    `BoundedAttributes` as immutable, which raises a `TypeError` on any write regardless of
883	    the end time. We temporarily clear that flag as well and restore it afterwards.
884	    """
885	    original_end_time = span._end_time
886	    span._end_time = None
887	    attributes = span._attributes
888	    original_immutable = getattr(attributes, "_immutable", None)
889	    if original_immutable is not None:
890	        attributes._immutable = False
891	    try:
892	        yield
893	    finally:
894	        span._end_time = original_end_time
895	        if original_immutable is not None:
896	            attributes._immutable = original_immutable

899	def parse_trace_id_v4(trace_id: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
900	    """

902	    """

906	        match trace_id.removeprefix(TRACE_ID_V4_PREFIX).split("/"):

198	def _fetch_traces_batch(
199	    trace_ids: list[str],
200	    tracking_store: AbstractStore,
201	) -> dict[str, Trace]:
202	    """
203	    Fetch traces in batch and return a mapping.
204	
205	    Attempts to load traces from the tracking store first. For any traces
206	    whose span data is stored in an artifact repository (e.g. S3) rather
207	    than in the tracking store, falls back to downloading from the artifact
208	    repository.
209	
210	    Args:
211	        trace_ids: List of trace IDs to fetch.
212	        tracking_store: The tracking store instance.
213	
214	    Returns:
215	        Dict mapping trace_id to Trace.
216	
217	    Raises:
218	        MlflowException: If any trace IDs are not found.
219	    """
220	    loader = OnlineTraceLoader(tracking_store)
221	    traces = loader.fetch_traces(trace_ids)
222	    trace_map = {t.info.trace_id: t for t in traces}
223	
224	    if missing_ids := [tid for tid in trace_ids if tid not in trace_map]:
225	        raise MlflowException(f"Traces not found: {missing_ids}")
226	
227	    return trace_map

230	def _run_session_scorer(
231	    scorer: Any,
232	    trace_ids: list[str],
233	    tracking_store: AbstractStore,
234	    log_assessments: bool,
235	) -> dict[str, TraceResult]:
236	    """
237	    Run a session-level scorer on all traces as a conversation.
238	
239	    Reuses evaluate_session_level_scorers from the evaluation harness.
240	
241	    Args:
242	        scorer: The scorer instance.
243	        trace_ids: List of trace IDs (representing a session).
244	        tracking_store: The tracking store instance.
245	        log_assessments: Whether to log assessments to the traces.
246	
247	    Returns:
248	        Dict mapping trace_id to TraceResult.
249	    """
250	    trace_map = _fetch_traces_batch(trace_ids, tracking_store)
251	
252	    # Preserve order of traces as requested
253	    traces = [trace_map[tid] for tid in trace_ids]
254	
255	    session_items = [EvalItem.from_trace(t) for t in traces]
256	
257	    # Get session_id from the first trace's metadata
258	    first_session_item = get_first_trace_in_session(session_items)
259	    trace_metadata = first_session_item.trace.info.trace_metadata or {}
260	    session_id = trace_metadata.get(TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION)
261	
262	    if not session_id:
263	        raise MlflowException(
264	            "Session-level scorer requires traces with session metadata. "
265	            f"Trace {first_session_item.trace.info.trace_id} is missing "
266	            f"'{TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION}' in its metadata."
267	        )
268	
269	    first_trace = first_session_item.trace
270	    first_trace_id = first_trace.info.trace_id
271	
272	    try:
273	        eval_result = evaluate_session_level_scorers(
274	            session_id=session_id,
275	            session_items=session_items,
276	            multi_turn_scorers=[scorer],
277	        )
278	
279	        feedbacks = eval_result.assessments
280	
281	        failures = _extract_failures_from_feedbacks(feedbacks)
282	
283	        if log_assessments and feedbacks:
284	            _log_assessments(
285	                run_id=None,  # No MLflow run context in API path
286	                trace=first_trace,
287	                assessments=feedbacks,
288	            )
289	
290	        return {
291	            first_trace_id: TraceResult(
292	                assessments=[f.to_dictionary() for f in feedbacks],
293	                failures=failures,
294	            )
295	        }
296	    except Exception as e:
297	        return {
298	            first_trace_id: TraceResult(
299	                failures=[ScorerFailure(error_code=type(e).__name__, error_message=str(e))]
300	            )
301	        }

304	def _run_single_turn_scorer_batch(
305	    scorer: Any,
306	    trace_ids: list[str],
307	    tracking_store: AbstractStore,
308	    log_assessments: bool,
309	) -> dict[str, TraceResult]:
310	    """
311	    Run a single-turn scorer on each trace in parallel.
312	
313	    Args:
314	        scorer: The scorer instance.
315	        trace_ids: List of trace IDs to evaluate.
316	        tracking_store: The tracking store instance.
317	        log_assessments: Whether to log assessments to the traces.
318	
319	    Returns:
320	        Dict mapping trace_id to TraceResult.
321	    """
322	    trace_map = _fetch_traces_batch(trace_ids, tracking_store)
323	
324	    def process_trace(trace_id: str, trace: Trace) -> tuple[str, TraceResult]:
325	        eval_item = EvalItem.from_trace(trace)
326	
327	        try:
328	            # Use _compute_eval_scores from harness - supports scorer tracing,
329	            # captures stack traces on errors
330	            result = _compute_eval_scores(
331	                eval_item=eval_item,
332	                scorers=[scorer],
333	            )
334	            feedbacks = result.assessments
335	
336	            failures = _extract_failures_from_feedbacks(feedbacks)
337	
338	            if log_assessments and feedbacks:
339	                _log_assessments(
340	                    run_id=None,  # No MLflow run context in API path
341	                    trace=trace,
342	                    assessments=feedbacks,
343	                )
344	
345	            return trace_id, TraceResult(
346	                assessments=[f.to_dictionary() for f in feedbacks],
347	                failures=failures,
348	            )
349	        except Exception as e:
350	            return trace_id, TraceResult(
351	                failures=[ScorerFailure(error_code=type(e).__name__, error_message=str(e))]
352	            )
353	
354	    max_workers = min(len(trace_map), MLFLOW_GENAI_EVAL_MAX_WORKERS.get())
355	    results: dict[str, TraceResult] = {}
356	
357	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(
358	        max_workers=max_workers,
359	        thread_name_prefix="MlflowScorerInvoke",
360	    ) as executor:
361	        futures = {
362	            executor.submit(process_trace, tid, trace): tid for tid, trace in trace_map.items()
363	        }
364	        for future in as_completed(futures):
365	            trace_id, result = future.result()
366	            results[trace_id] = result
367	
368	    return results

371	def _group_traces_by_session_id(
372	    trace_ids: list[str],
373	    tracking_store: AbstractStore,
374	) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
375	    """
376	    Group trace_ids by their session_id metadata.
377	
378	    Fetches trace info from the tracking store and groups them by session_id.
379	    Traces without a session_id are skipped.
380	
381	    Args:
382	        trace_ids: List of trace IDs to group.
383	        tracking_store: The tracking store instance.
384	
385	    Returns:
386	        Dictionary mapping session_id to list of trace_ids, sorted by timestamp.
387	    """
388	    session_groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
389	    # trace_id -> (session_id, timestamp_ms)
390	    trace_info_cache: dict[str, tuple[str, int | None]] = {}
391	
392	    trace_infos = tracking_store.batch_get_trace_infos(trace_ids)
393	
394	    for trace_info in trace_infos:
395	        trace_metadata = trace_info.trace_metadata or {}
396	        if session_id := trace_metadata.get(TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION):
397	            if session_id not in session_groups:
398	                session_groups[session_id] = []
399	            session_groups[session_id].append(trace_info.trace_id)
400	            trace_info_cache[trace_info.trace_id] = (session_id, trace_info.timestamp_ms)
401	
402	    # Sort trace_ids within each session by trace timestamp (None timestamps sort last)
403	    for session_id in session_groups:
404	        session_groups[session_id] = sorted(
405	            session_groups[session_id],
406	            key=lambda tid: trace_info_cache.get(tid, ("", None))[1] or float("inf"),
407	        )
408	
409	    return session_groups
410

412	def get_trace_batches_for_scorer(
413	    trace_ids: list[str],
414	    scorer: Scorer,
415	    tracking_store: AbstractStore,
416	) -> list[list[str]]:
417	    """
418	    Get trace ID batches for scorer invocation.
419	
420	    Handles batching logic for both session-level and single-turn scorers:
421	    - Session-level scorers: Groups traces by session_id, returns one batch per session.
422	    - Single-turn scorers: Batches traces based on MLFLOW_SERVER_SCORER_INVOKE_BATCH_SIZE.
423	
424	    Args:
425	        trace_ids: List of trace IDs to evaluate.
426	        scorer: The validated Scorer instance.
427	        tracking_store: The tracking store instance.
428	
429	    Returns:
430	        List of trace ID batches, where each batch should be submitted as a separate job.
431	    """
432	    if scorer.is_session_level_scorer:
433	        # For conversation judges, group traces by session_id
434	        session_groups = _group_traces_by_session_id(trace_ids, tracking_store)
435	        return list(session_groups.values())
436	    else:
437	        # For single-turn judges, batch traces into fixed-size batches
438	        batch_size = MLFLOW_SERVER_SCORER_INVOKE_BATCH_SIZE.get()
439	        return [trace_ids[i : i + batch_size] for i in range(0, len(trace_ids), batch_size)]

442	def run_online_scoring_scheduler() -> None:
443	    """
444	    Periodic task that fetches active online scorers and submits scoring jobs.
445	
446	    Groups scorers by experiment_id and submits two jobs per experiment:
447	    1. Trace-level scoring job for single-turn scorers
448	    2. Session-level scoring job for session scorers
449	
450	    Groups are shuffled to prevent starvation when there are limited job runners available.
451	    """
452	    tracking_store = _get_tracking_store()
453	    # Iterate on each workspaces in the tracking store to run all registered scorers
454	    for workspace_ctx in _get_online_scoring_workspace_contexts():
455	        with workspace_ctx as workspace:
456	            online_scorers = tracking_store.get_active_online_scorers()
457	            workspace_label = f" in workspace '{workspace}'" if workspace else ""
458	            _logger.debug(
459	                f"Online scoring scheduler found {len(online_scorers)} active scorers"
460	                f"{workspace_label}"
461	            )
462	
463	            scorers_by_experiment: dict[str, list[OnlineScorer]] = defaultdict(list)
464	            for scorer in online_scorers:
465	                scorers_by_experiment[scorer.online_config.experiment_id].append(scorer)
466	
467	            # Shuffle configs randomly to prevent scorer starvation when there are
468	            # limited job runners available
469	            experiment_groups = list(scorers_by_experiment.items())
470	            random.shuffle(experiment_groups)
471	            _logger.debug(
472	                f"Grouped into {len(experiment_groups)} experiments, submitting jobs per experiment"
473	            )
474	
475	            for experiment_id, scorers in experiment_groups:
476	                # Separate scorers by type
477	                session_level_scorers = []
478	                trace_level_scorers = []
479	
480	                for scorer in scorers:
481	                    try:
482	                        scorer_obj = Scorer.model_validate_json(scorer.serialized_scorer)
483	                        if scorer_obj.is_session_level_scorer:
484	                            session_level_scorers.append(scorer)
485	                        else:
486	                            trace_level_scorers.append(scorer)
487	                    except Exception as e:
488	                        _logger.warning(
489	                            f"Failed to load scorer '{scorer.name}'; scorer will be skipped: {e}"
490	                        )
491	
492	                # Only submit jobs for scorer types that exist
493	                if trace_level_scorers:
494	                    _logger.debug(
495	                        f"Submitting trace scoring job for experiment {experiment_id} "
496	                        f"with {len(trace_level_scorers)} scorers"
497	                    )
498	                    trace_scorer_dicts = [asdict(scorer) for scorer in trace_level_scorers]
499	                    submit_job(
500	                        run_online_trace_scorer_job,
501	                        {"experiment_id": experiment_id, "online_scorers": trace_scorer_dicts},
502	                    )
503	
504	                if session_level_scorers:
505	                    _logger.debug(
506	                        f"Submitting session scoring job for experiment {experiment_id} "
507	                        f"with {len(session_level_scorers)} scorers"
508	                    )
509	                    session_scorer_dicts = [asdict(scorer) for scorer in session_level_scorers]
510	                    submit_job(
511	                        run_online_session_scorer_job,
512	                        {"experiment_id": experiment_id, "online_scorers": session_scorer_dicts},
513	                    )
514	
515	
516	def _get_online_scoring_workspace_contexts():
517	    if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_WORKSPACES.get():
518	        return [nullcontext()]
519	
520	    from mlflow.server.workspace_helpers import _get_workspace_store  # avoid circular import
521	
522	    store = _get_workspace_store()
523	    workspaces = list(store.list_workspaces())
524	    if not workspaces:
525	        _logger.info("Online scoring scheduler found no workspaces; skipping.")
526	        return []
527	
528	    return [WorkspaceContext(workspace.name) for workspace in workspaces]

137	class MemoryAugmentedJudge(Judge):
138	    """
139	    A judge augmented with dual memory systems.
140	
141	    This judge enhances evaluation with:
142	    - Semantic Memory: Distilled guidelines from past feedback
143	    - Episodic Memory: Retrieved similar examples from past feedback
144	
145	    The judge maintains state across evaluations and provides the exact same
146	    interface as the original judge. Memories are managed internally.
147	
148	    Args:
149	        base_judge: Base judge to augment with memory systems
150	        reflection_lm: {{ reflection_lm }}
151	        retrieval_k: Number of similar examples to retrieve from episodic memory (default: 5)
152	        embedding_model: {{ embedding_model }}
153	        embedding_dim: Dimension of embeddings (default: 512)
154	    """
155	
156	    def __init__(
157	        self,
158	        base_judge: Judge,
159	        reflection_lm: str | None = None,
160	        retrieval_k: int = 5,
161	        embedding_model: str | None = None,
162	        embedding_dim: int = 512,
163	        *,
164	        _defer_init: bool = False,
165	    ):
166	        # Input validation
167	        if not isinstance(retrieval_k, int) or retrieval_k <= 0:
168	            raise MlflowException(
169	                f"retrieval_k must be a positive integer, got {retrieval_k}",
170	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
171	            )
172	
173	        if not isinstance(embedding_dim, int) or embedding_dim <= 0:
174	            raise MlflowException(
175	                f"embedding_dim must be a positive integer, got {embedding_dim}",
176	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
177	            )
178	
179	        effective_base_judge = (
180	            base_judge._base_judge if isinstance(base_judge, MemoryAugmentedJudge) else base_judge
181	        )
182	
183	        super().__init__(
184	            name=effective_base_judge.name,
185	            description=effective_base_judge.description,
186	            aggregations=effective_base_judge.aggregations,
187	        )
188	
189	        self._base_judge = effective_base_judge
190	        self._retrieval_k = retrieval_k
191	        self._reflection_lm = reflection_lm if reflection_lm is not None else get_default_model()
192	        self._embedding_model = (
193	            embedding_model if embedding_model is not None else get_default_embedding_model()
194	        )
195	        self._embedding_dim = embedding_dim
196	
197	        # Always store trace IDs for serialization
198	        self._episodic_trace_ids: list[str] = []
199	
200	        if _defer_init:
201	            # Defer creating heavyweight DSPy objects until first use (_embedder=None signals this)
202	            self._base_signature = None
203	            self._embedder = None
204	            self._retriever = None
205	            self._episodic_memory: list["dspy.Example"] = []
206	            self._semantic_memory: list[Guideline] = []
207	        else:
208	            self._initialize_dspy_components(base_judge)
209	
210	    def _initialize_dspy_components(self, base_judge: Judge | None = None) -> None:
211	        """Initialize heavyweight DSPy components (embedder, memory index)."""
212	        effective_base_judge = base_judge or self._base_judge
213	
214	        self._base_signature = create_dspy_signature(effective_base_judge)
215	        self._embedder = _build_embedder(self._embedding_model, self._embedding_dim)
216	        self._retriever = None
217	
218	        # Inherit memory from base_judge if it's a MemoryAugmentedJudge.
219	        # Episodic memory index is not built here — _add_examples_to_memory() handles it.
220	        if isinstance(base_judge, MemoryAugmentedJudge):
221	            self._semantic_memory = copy.deepcopy(base_judge._semantic_memory)
222	            self._episodic_trace_ids = base_judge._episodic_trace_ids.copy()
223	            if base_judge._episodic_memory:
224	                self._episodic_memory = copy.deepcopy(base_judge._episodic_memory)
225	            elif self._episodic_trace_ids:
226	                self._episodic_memory = self._reconstruct_episodic_memory()
227	            else:
228	                self._episodic_memory: list["dspy.Example"] = []
229	        else:
230	            self._episodic_memory: list["dspy.Example"] = []
231	            self._semantic_memory: list[Guideline] = []
232	
233	    def __call__(
234	        self,
235	        *,
236	        inputs: Any = None,
237	        outputs: Any = None,
238	        expectations: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
239	        trace: Trace | None = None,
240	    ) -> Assessment:
241	        self._lazy_init()
242	
243	        if trace is not None:
244	            inputs = resolve_inputs_from_trace(inputs, trace)
245	            outputs = resolve_outputs_from_trace(outputs, trace)
246	            expectations = resolve_expectations_from_trace(expectations, trace)
247	
248	        guidelines = [g.guideline_text for g in self._semantic_memory]
249	        query_kwargs = {
250	            "inputs": inputs,
251	            "outputs": outputs,
252	            "expectations": expectations,
253	            "trace": trace,
254	        }
255	        retrieved_results = retrieve_relevant_examples(
256	            retriever=self._retriever,
257	            examples=self._episodic_memory,
258	            query_kwargs=query_kwargs,
259	            signature=self._base_signature,
260	        )
261	
262	        relevant_examples = [example for example, _ in retrieved_results]
263	        retrieved_trace_ids = [trace_id for _, trace_id in retrieved_results]
264	
265	        # Score through a per-call copy of the base judge: this preserves its invocation flow
266	        # (agentic tool-calling for {{ trace }} judges) while keeping the retrieved examples,
267	        # which differ per call, off the judge shared by concurrently scored rows. The copy is
268	        # shallow because only _instructions is reassigned; nested state is never mutated.
269	        scoring_judge = self._base_judge.model_copy()
270	        scoring_judge._instructions = self._build_augmented_instructions(
271	            guidelines, relevant_examples
272	        )
273	
274	        prediction = scoring_judge(
275	            inputs=inputs,
276	            outputs=outputs,
277	            expectations=expectations,
278	            trace=trace,
279	        )
280	
281	        # Reset metadata["guideline"], which the UI renders as a short per-assertion label, to
282	        # the base criterion so retrieved examples aren't persisted onto every assessment.
283	        metadata = {**(prediction.metadata or {})}
284	        if "guideline" in metadata:
285	            metadata["guideline"] = self._base_judge.instructions
286	        if retrieved_trace_ids:
287	            metadata["retrieved_example_trace_ids"] = retrieved_trace_ids
288	        prediction.metadata = metadata
289	
290	        return prediction

292	    def _build_augmented_instructions(
293	        self,
294	        guidelines: list[str],
295	        examples: list["dspy.Example"],
296	    ) -> str:
297	        """Build instructions augmented with MemAlign guidelines and retrieved examples.
298	
299	        Section order (examples, then guidelines) and header wording match the DSPy
300	        signature this replaced, whose fields were prepended in that order.
301	        """
302	        parts = [self._base_judge.instructions]
303	
304	        if examples:
305	            parts.append(f"\n\nExample Judgements ({len(examples)}):")
306	            parts.append(EXAMPLES_SECTION_HEADER)
307	            for i, example in enumerate(examples, 1):
308	                example_dict = {
309	                    k: v for k, v in example.items() if not k.startswith("dspy_") and k != "trace"
310	                }
311	                if hasattr(example, "trace") and example.trace is not None:
312	                    example_dict["trace"] = value_to_embedding_text(example.trace)
313	                parts.append(f"  Example {i}: {example_dict}")
314	
315	        if guidelines:
316	            parts.append(f"\n\nDistilled Guidelines ({len(guidelines)}):")
317	            parts.append(GUIDELINES_SECTION_HEADER)
318	            parts.extend(f"  - {guideline}" for guideline in guidelines)
319	
320	        return "\n".join(parts)

399	    def _create_copy(self) -> "MemoryAugmentedJudge":
400	        """
401	        Override base _create_copy for Scorer.register().

403	        The base implementation uses model_copy(deep=True), which fails because
404	        DSPy objects (_embedder, _retriever) contain thread locks that can't be
405	        pickled. We create a new instance with _defer_init=True and store trace
406	        IDs for lazy reconstruction.
407	        """
408	        judge_copy = MemoryAugmentedJudge(
409	            base_judge=self._base_judge,
410	            reflection_lm=self._reflection_lm,
411	            retrieval_k=self._retrieval_k,

421	    def _reconstruct_episodic_memory(self) -> list["dspy.Example"]:
422	        examples = []
423	        missing_ids = []
424	        for trace_id in self._episodic_trace_ids:
425	            trace = mlflow.get_trace(trace_id, silent=True)
426	            if trace is not None:
427	                examples.extend(trace_to_dspy_example(trace, self._base_judge))
428	            else:
429	                missing_ids.append(trace_id)
430	
431	        if missing_ids:
432	            _logger.warning(
433	                f"Could not find {len(missing_ids)} traces for episodic memory reconstruction. "
434	                f"Missing trace IDs: {missing_ids[:5]}"
435	                f"{'...' if len(missing_ids) > 5 else ''}. "
436	                f"Judge will operate with partial memory "
437	                f"({len(examples)}/{len(self._episodic_trace_ids)} traces)."
438	            )
439	
440	        return examples

442	    def _lazy_init(self) -> None:
443	        """
444	        Lazily initialize DSPy components and episodic memory from stored trace IDs.
445	
446	        This method is called on first use (e.g., __call__) when the judge was created
447	        with _defer_init=True. It:
448	        1. Creates the embedder
449	        2. Fetches traces by ID and reconstructs episodic memory
450	        3. Builds the episodic memory search index
451	
452	        No-op if already initialized (checked via _embedder not being None).
453	        """
454	        if self._embedder is not None:
455	            return
456	
457	        self._base_signature = create_dspy_signature(self._base_judge)
458	
459	        self._embedder = _build_embedder(self._embedding_model, self._embedding_dim)
460	
461	        self._episodic_memory = self._reconstruct_episodic_memory()
462	
463	        if self._episodic_memory:
464	            self._build_episodic_memory()
