466	    def unalign(self, traces: list[Trace]) -> "MemoryAugmentedJudge":
467	        """
468	        Remove specific traces from memory and return an updated judge.
469	
470	        This method allows you to selectively remove feedback examples from the judge's
471	        memory systems. This is useful when you want to:
472	
473	        - Remove incorrect or low-quality feedback that negatively impacts performance
474	        - Update the judge in case your evaluation criteria change
475	        - Remove feedback from specific users or time periods
476	
477	        The returned judge will have guidelines selectively deleted based on source_trace_ids:
478	        - Guidelines where all source traces were removed are deleted
479	        - Guidelines with at least one remaining source trace are retained
480	
481	        Args:
482	            traces: Traces containing feedback to remove from memory. Only traces with
483	                feedback matching this judge's name will be removed.
484	
485	        Returns:
486	            Updated MemoryAugmentedJudge with specified traces removed from memory.
487	
488	        Example:
489	            .. code-block:: python
490	
491	                import mlflow
492	                from mlflow.genai.judges import make_judge
493	                from mlflow.genai.judges.optimizers import MemAlignOptimizer
494	
495	                # Assuming `all_traces` contains human feedback for the judge
496	                aligned_judge = judge.align(traces=all_traces, optimizer=MemAlignOptimizer())
497	                aligned_judge_v2 = aligned_judge.unalign(traces=bad_traces)
498	                # aligned_judge_v2 now only retains feedback from
499	                # `set(all_traces) - set(bad_traces)`
500	        """
501	        # A judge loaded from the registry holds only trace IDs until its episodic memory is
502	        # reconstructed. Without this, the check below would find nothing to remove and
503	        # silently return an unchanged judge that still contains the retracted feedback.
504	        self._lazy_init()
505	
506	        trace_ids_to_remove = {trace.info.trace_id for trace in traces}
507	
508	        if not any(
509	            getattr(ex, "_trace_id", None) in trace_ids_to_remove for ex in self._episodic_memory
510	        ):
511	            _logger.warning("No feedback records found for the provided traces")
512	            return self
513	
514	        new_judge = MemoryAugmentedJudge(
515	            base_judge=self._base_judge,
516	            reflection_lm=self._reflection_lm,
517	            retrieval_k=self._retrieval_k,
518	            embedding_model=self._embedding_model,
519	            embedding_dim=self._embedding_dim,
520	        )
521	        new_judge._episodic_memory = list(self._episodic_memory)
522	        new_judge._episodic_trace_ids = list(self._episodic_trace_ids)
523	        new_judge._semantic_memory = copy.deepcopy(self._semantic_memory)
524	
525	        new_judge._apply_unalign_inplace(trace_ids_to_remove)
526	        new_judge._build_episodic_memory()
527	
528	        _logger.debug(
529	            f"Removed {len(traces)} traces from memory. "
530	            f"Episodic memory size: {len(new_judge._episodic_memory)} examples, "
531	            f"Semantic memory size: {len(new_judge._semantic_memory)} guidelines."
532	        )
533	        return new_judge
534	
535	    def _in_memory_fingerprint(self, trace_id: str) -> frozenset[tuple[str | None, int | None]]:
536	        return _generate_fingerprint(
537	            ex for ex in self._episodic_memory if getattr(ex, "_trace_id", None) == trace_id
538	        )
539	
540	    def _apply_unalign_inplace(self, trace_ids_to_remove: set[str]) -> None:
541	        # Mutates self; does not rebuild the episodic search index (caller's responsibility).
542	        self._episodic_memory = [
543	            ex
544	            for ex in self._episodic_memory
545	            if getattr(ex, "_trace_id", None) not in trace_ids_to_remove
546	        ]
547	        self._episodic_trace_ids = [
548	            tid for tid in self._episodic_trace_ids if tid not in trace_ids_to_remove
549	        ]
550	        # Drop a guideline only when ALL of its source traces are being removed —
551	        # i.e., retain ``g`` if ``source_trace_ids`` has at least one tid outside the
552	        # remove set, or if it has no recorded sources (user-provided guidelines).
553	        # A cross-trace guideline aggregates signal from each of its source traces,
554	        # so refreshing one source doesn't invalidate the signal that came from the
555	        # others.
556	        self._semantic_memory = [
557	            g
558	            for g in self._semantic_memory
559	            if g.source_trace_ids is None
560	            or any(tid not in trace_ids_to_remove for tid in g.source_trace_ids)
561	        ]
562	
563	    def _distill_new_guidelines(self, new_examples: list["dspy.Example"]) -> None:
564	        """
565	        Distill new guidelines from newly added examples and add to semantic memory.
566	
567	        Args:
568	            new_examples: The examples that were just added (not all examples)
569	        """
570	        existing_guideline_texts = [g.guideline_text for g in self._semantic_memory]
571	        new_guidelines = distill_guidelines(
572	            examples=new_examples,
573	            judge_instructions=self._base_judge.instructions,
574	            reflection_lm=self._reflection_lm,
575	            existing_guidelines=existing_guideline_texts,
576	        )
577	        self._semantic_memory.extend(new_guidelines)
578	        _logger.debug(
579	            f"Distilled {len(new_guidelines)} new guidelines from {len(new_examples)} new "
580	            f"examples. Semantic memory now has {len(self._semantic_memory)} guidelines."
581	        )
582	
583	    def _build_episodic_memory(self) -> None:
584	        """Build episodic memory search index from examples."""
585	        import dspy.retrievers
586	
587	        query_field = get_query_field(self._base_signature)
588	        if query_field is None:
589	            raise MlflowException(
590	                "Unable to build episodic memory: no suitable input field found in judge "
591	                "instructions. Please ensure the judge instructions reference at least one of "
592	                "the following fields: inputs, outputs, expectations, conversation, trace.",
593	                error_code=INTERNAL_ERROR,
594	            )
595	
596	        # Build corpus and filter examples with empty query field
597	        filtered_memory = []
598	        corpus = []
599	        for example in self._episodic_memory:
600	            if value := getattr(example, query_field, None):
601	                query = truncate_to_token_limit(
602	                    value_to_embedding_text(value), self._embedding_model, model_type="embedding"
603	                )
604	                corpus.append(query)
605	                filtered_memory.append(example)
606	        self._episodic_memory = filtered_memory
607	
608	        self._retriever = dspy.retrievers.Embeddings(
609	            embedder=self._embedder, corpus=corpus, k=self._retrieval_k
610	        )
611	        _logger.debug(f"Episodic memory corpus contains {len(corpus)} examples")
612	
613	    def _add_examples_to_memory(self, examples: list["dspy.Example"]) -> None:
614	        """Add examples by updating both episodic memory and semantic memory.
615	
616	        Args:
617	            examples: Examples to add
618	        """
619	        # Update episodic memory and trace IDs
620	        self._episodic_memory.extend(examples)
621	        self._episodic_trace_ids.extend(ex._trace_id for ex in examples if hasattr(ex, "_trace_id"))
622	        self._build_episodic_memory()
623	
624	        # Update semantic memory
625	        self._distill_new_guidelines(examples)

629	class MemAlignOptimizer(AlignmentOptimizer):
630	    """
631	    MemAlign alignment optimizer using dual memory systems.
632	
633	    This optimizer creates a memory-augmented judge that learns from feedback
634	    through two complementary mechanisms:
635	
636	    **Semantic Memory** - Distills general guidelines from feedback:
637	        - LLM extracts patterns from feedback records
638	        - Guidelines describe user preferences and expectations
639	        - Applied as context to all future evaluations
640	
641	    **Episodic Memory** - Retrieves similar past examples:
642	        - Stores feedback records with embeddings
643	        - Finds most similar examples during evaluation
644	        - Provides concrete examples as evaluation context
645	
646	    The returned judge is a MemoryAugmentedJudge that maintains memory state.
647	
648	    Args:
649	        reflection_lm: {{ reflection_lm }}
650	        retrieval_k: Number of similar examples to retrieve from episodic memory (default: 5)
651	        embedding_model: {{ embedding_model }}
652	        embedding_dim: Dimension of embeddings (default: 512)
653	
654	    Note:
655	        The number of parallel threads for LLM calls during guideline distillation can be
656	        configured via the ``MLFLOW_GENAI_OPTIMIZE_MAX_WORKERS`` environment variable
657	        (default: 8). Increasing this value can speed up alignment when processing many
658	        feedback examples, but may increase API rate limit errors.
659	
660	    Example:
661	        .. code-block:: python
662	
663	            import mlflow
664	            from mlflow.genai.judges import make_judge
665	            from mlflow.genai.judges.optimizers import MemAlignOptimizer
666	
667	            judge = make_judge(name="quality", instructions="...", model="openai:/gpt-4")
668	            optimizer = MemAlignOptimizer(
669	                reflection_lm="openai:/gpt-4o-mini",
670	                retrieval_k=3,
671	                embedding_model="openai:/text-embedding-3-small",
672	            )
673	
674	            # Assuming `traces` contains human feedback for the judge
675	            optimized_judge = judge.align(traces=traces, optimizer=optimizer)
676	            result = optimized_judge(inputs="...", outputs="...")
677	    """
678	
679	    def __init__(
680	        self,
681	        reflection_lm: str | None = None,
682	        retrieval_k: int = 5,
683	        embedding_model: str | None = None,
684	        embedding_dim: int = 512,
685	    ):
686	        _check_dspy_installed()
687	        self._reflection_lm = reflection_lm if reflection_lm is not None else get_default_model()
688	        self._retrieval_k = retrieval_k
689	        self._embedding_model = (
690	            embedding_model if embedding_model is not None else get_default_embedding_model()
691	        )
692	        self._embedding_dim = embedding_dim
693	
694	    def align(self, judge: Judge, traces: list[Trace]) -> MemoryAugmentedJudge:
695	        """
696	        Align a judge with human feedback from traces.
697	
698	        When ``judge`` is already a :py:class:`MemoryAugmentedJudge` (e.g., the
699	        result of a prior ``align`` call), per-trace behavior is:
700	
701	        - Traces whose human assessments are byte-identical to what is already
702	          in memory are skipped — no LM call, no index rebuild.
703	        - Traces in memory whose assessments have been edited, added, or
704	          partially removed are refreshed: stale episodes are dropped and
705	          replaced with examples derived from the current trace state.
706	        - Traces not yet in memory are added.
707	        - Traces whose human assessments have been *fully* removed raise
708	          :py:class:`MlflowException`. To remove a trace's contribution to
709	          memory, call :py:meth:`MemoryAugmentedJudge.unalign` directly —
710	          re-aligning with empty assessments is not a supported retraction
711	          path. Likewise, traces that have never had any human assessments
712	          for ``judge.name`` raise rather than being silently skipped.
713	
714	        Args:
715	            judge: Judge to align (or re-align if already a
716	                :py:class:`MemoryAugmentedJudge`).
717	            traces: Traces containing human feedback.
718	
719	        Returns:
720	            Memory-augmented judge aligned with feedback.
721	        """
722	        try:
723	            if not traces:
724	                raise MlflowException(
725	                    "No traces provided for alignment", error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
726	                )
727	
728	            _logger.debug(f"Starting MemAlign alignment with {len(traces)} traces")
729	
730	            memory_judge = MemoryAugmentedJudge(
731	                base_judge=judge,
732	                reflection_lm=self._reflection_lm,
733	                retrieval_k=self._retrieval_k,
734	                embedding_model=self._embedding_model,
735	                embedding_dim=self._embedding_dim,
736	            )
737	
738	            # Build resolved examples once per incoming trace; reused for both change
739	            # detection and memory updates. Last-write-wins on duplicate trace_ids gives
740	            # us in-batch dedup for free (handles align(judge, [t, t])).
741	            examples_by_trace = {
742	                trace.info.trace_id: trace_to_dspy_example(trace, judge) for trace in traces
743	            }
744	
745	            # Classify each trace as: emptied-from-memory (retraction attempt),
746	            # never-had-feedback (user error), skip (identical to memory), refresh
747	            # (in memory but assessments changed), or new (not in memory).
748	            trace_ids_with_empty_assessments: set[str] = set()
749	            trace_ids_with_no_feedback: set[str] = set()
750	            trace_ids_to_refresh: set[str] = set()
751	            examples_to_align: list["dspy.Example"] = []
752	            for tid, examples in examples_by_trace.items():
753	                new_fp = _generate_fingerprint(examples)
754	                old_fp = memory_judge._in_memory_fingerprint(tid)
755	                if not examples:
756	                    # Any trace that resolves to zero examples blocks the call. We
757	                    # split the two cases so the error message points at the right
758	                    # remediation: unalign() for retraction, log_feedback() for
759	                    # missing feedback. Both are loud rather than silently dropped
760	                    # because mixing one with valid traces would otherwise hide a
761	                    # likely user bug (wrong trace IDs / missing feedback / etc.).
762	                    if old_fp:
763	                        trace_ids_with_empty_assessments.add(tid)
764	                    else:
765	                        trace_ids_with_no_feedback.add(tid)
766	                elif not old_fp:
767	                    examples_to_align.extend(examples)
768	                elif old_fp != new_fp:
769	                    trace_ids_to_refresh.add(tid)
770	                    examples_to_align.extend(examples)
771	
772	            if trace_ids_with_empty_assessments:
773	                raise MlflowException(
774	                    f"Cannot retract feedback by re-aligning with empty assessments. "
775	                    f"{len(trace_ids_with_empty_assessments)} trace(s) had their human "
776	                    f"assessments removed: {sorted(trace_ids_with_empty_assessments)}. "
777	                    f"Use unalign(traces=...) to remove traces from memory.",
778	                    error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
779	                )
780	
781	            if trace_ids_with_no_feedback:
782	                raise MlflowException(
783	                    f"No valid feedback records found for {len(trace_ids_with_no_feedback)} "
784	                    f"trace(s): {sorted(trace_ids_with_no_feedback)}. Ensure traces contain "
785	                    f"human assessments with name '{judge.name}'.",
786	                    error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
787	                )
788	
789	            if not examples_to_align:
790	                # Reachable only when every incoming trace was a no-op skip; the
791	                # raises above already cover all empty-example paths. Skip can
792	                # only fire when ``judge`` is already a MemoryAugmentedJudge — a
793	                # vanilla Judge has no in-memory fingerprints to match against —
794	                # so returning the input is type-safe and avoids handing back the
795	                # freshly-built ``memory_judge`` whose retriever is uninitialized.
796	                assert isinstance(judge, MemoryAugmentedJudge)
797	                _logger.debug("MemAlign alignment skipped: all traces unchanged in memory.")
798	                return judge
799	
800	            if trace_ids_to_refresh:
801	                memory_judge._apply_unalign_inplace(trace_ids_to_refresh)
802	
803	            memory_judge._add_examples_to_memory(examples_to_align)
804	
805	            _logger.debug(
806	                f"MemAlign alignment completed: "
807	                f"refreshed={len(trace_ids_to_refresh)}, "
808	                f"added={len(examples_to_align)} examples."
809	            )
810	            return memory_judge
811	
812	        except Exception as e:
813	            _logger.error(f"MemAlign alignment failed: {e}", exc_info=True)
814	            raise MlflowException(
815	                f"Alignment optimization failed: {e!s}", error_code=INTERNAL_ERROR
816	            ) from e

50	@contextmanager
51	def suppress_verbose_logging(
52	    logger_name: str, threshold_level: int = logging.DEBUG
53	) -> Iterator[None]:
54	    """
55	    Context manager to suppress verbose logging from a specific logger.
56	
57	    This is useful when running optimization algorithms that produce verbose output
58	    by default. The suppression only applies if the parent MLflow logger is above
59	    the threshold level, allowing users to see detailed output when they explicitly
60	    set logging to DEBUG.
61	
62	    Args:
63	        logger_name: Name of the logger to control.
64	        threshold_level: Only suppress if MLflow logger is above this level.
65	            Defaults to logging.DEBUG.
66	
67	    Example:
68	        >>> with suppress_verbose_logging("some.verbose.library"):
69	        ...     # Run operations that would normally log verbosely
70	        ...     result = run_optimization()
71	    """
72	    logger = logging.getLogger(logger_name)
73	    original_level = logger.level
74	    try:
75	        if _logger.getEffectiveLevel() > threshold_level:
76	            logger.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
77	        yield
78	    finally:
79	        logger.setLevel(original_level)

82	def create_gepa_metric_adapter(
83	    metric_fn: Callable[["dspy.Example", Any, Any | None], bool],
84	) -> Any:
85	    """
86	    Create a metric adapter that bridges DSPy's standard metric to GEPA's format.
87	
88	    GEPA requires a metric with signature: (gold, pred, trace, pred_name, pred_trace)
89	    but our standard metric_fn has signature: (example, pred, trace).
90	    This function creates an adapter that bridges the two signatures.
91	
92	    Args:
93	        metric_fn: Standard metric function with signature (example, pred, trace)
94	
95	    Returns:
96	        Adapter function with GEPA's expected signature
97	    """
98	
99	    def gepa_metric_adapter(gold, pred, trace=None, pred_name=None, pred_trace=None):
100	        """Adapt DSPy's 3-argument metric to GEPA's 5-argument format."""
101	        # gold is the dspy.Example
102	        # pred is the prediction output
103	        # trace/pred_name/pred_trace are optional GEPA-specific args
104	        # We pass None for our metric's trace parameter since GEPA's trace is different
105	        return metric_fn(gold, pred, trace=None)
106	
107	    return gepa_metric_adapter

159	def _get_databricks_api_base_key(model_name: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
160	    """
161	    Get the api_base URL and api_key for a Databricks-hosted model.
162	
163	    Databricks serves OpenAI-compatible models through two surfaces, selected by the shape
164	    of ``model_name``:
165	
166	    * Legacy model serving (``https://<host>/serving-endpoints``) for serving endpoints
167	      referenced by their simple name (e.g. ``databricks-claude-haiku-4-5``).
168	    * Mosaic AI Gateway (``https://<host>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1``) for foundation models
169	      referenced by their Unity Catalog name (e.g. ``system.ai.claude-haiku-4-5``).
170	
171	    In both cases LiteLLM appends ``/chat/completions`` (or ``/embeddings``) to ``api_base``
172	    and passes ``model_name`` in the request body, so the final URL is, e.g.,
173	    ``https://<host>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`` with
174	    ``model=system.ai.claude-haiku-4-5``.
175	
176	    Args:
177	        model_name: The model/endpoint name parsed from the MLflow URI (the part after
178	            ``databricks:/`` or ``endpoints:/``).
179	
180	    Returns:
181	        Tuple of (api_base, api_key) - both None if credentials cannot be determined
182	    """
183	    # Get Databricks host and token from environment or SDK
184	    host = os.environ.get("DATABRICKS_HOST")
185	    api_key = os.environ.get("DATABRICKS_TOKEN")
186	
187	    if not host or not api_key:
188	        try:
189	            from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient
190	        except ImportError:
191	            _logger.warning(
192	                "Could not determine Databricks credentials. "
193	                "Set DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN environment variables."
194	            )
195	            return None, None
196	
197	        client = WorkspaceClient()
198	        if not host:
199	            host = client.config.host
200	        if not api_key:
201	            # Get token from SDK authentication (supports OAuth, PAT, etc.)
202	            headers = client.config.authenticate()
203	            if "Authorization" in headers:
204	                api_key = headers["Authorization"].replace("Bearer ", "")
205	
206	    if not host:
207	        return None, None
208	
209	    host = host.rstrip("/")
210	    # Unity Catalog models live behind the AI Gateway; everything else is a serving endpoint.
211	    # LiteLLM appends /chat/completions (or /embeddings) and passes the model name in the body.
212	    base_path = (
213	        _DATABRICKS_AI_GATEWAY_PATH
214	        if _is_unity_catalog_model_name(model_name)
215	        else _DATABRICKS_SERVING_ENDPOINTS_PATH
216	    )
217	    return f"{host}/{base_path}", api_key

320	    LiteLLM uses formats like 'openai/gpt-4' while MLflow expects 'openai:/gpt-4'.

322	    Args:
323	        litellm_model: LiteLLM model string (e.g., 'openai/gpt-4')

335	        'anthropic:/claude-3'

363	def _resolve_assessment_conflicts(assessments: list["Assessment"]) -> list["Assessment"]:
364	    if not assessments:
365	        return []
366	
367	    groups: dict[str, list["Assessment"]] = defaultdict(list)
368	    for assessment in assessments:
369	        if assessment.feedback:
370	            label = str(assessment.feedback.value).lower()
371	            groups[label].append(assessment)
372	
373	    if len(groups) == 1:
374	        return assessments
375	
376	    def group_priority(label: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
377	        group = groups[label]
378	        return len(group), max(a.create_time_ms or 0 for a in group)
379	
380	    winning_label = max(groups, key=group_priority)
381	    return groups[winning_label]

384	def trace_to_dspy_example(trace: Trace, judge: Judge) -> list["dspy.Example"]:
385	    """
386	    Convert MLflow trace to DSPy example format.
387	
388	    When multiple human assessments with the same judge name exist on a trace:
389	    - If all assessments agree on the label: returns an example for each assessment
390	    - If there's a conflict: returns examples only for the majority label
391	    - If there's a tie: returns examples for the group with the most recent assessment
392	
393	    Extracts:
394	    - inputs/outputs from trace spans
395	    - expected result from human assessments
396	    - rationale from assessment feedback
397	
398	    Args:
399	        trace: MLflow trace object
400	        judge: Judge instance to find assessments for
401	
402	    Returns:
403	        List of DSPy example objects (empty list if no valid assessments found)
404	    """
405	    try:
406	        judge_input_fields = judge.get_input_fields()
407	
408	        judge_requires_trace = any(field.name == "trace" for field in judge_input_fields)
409	        judge_requires_inputs = any(field.name == "inputs" for field in judge_input_fields)
410	        judge_requires_outputs = any(field.name == "outputs" for field in judge_input_fields)
411	        judge_requires_expectations = any(
412	            field.name == "expectations" for field in judge_input_fields
413	        )

415	        request = extract_request_from_trace(trace)
416	        response = extract_response_from_trace(trace)
417	        expectations = extract_expectations_from_trace(trace)
418	
419	        # Check for missing required fields
420	        if not request and judge_requires_inputs:
421	            _logger.warning(f"Missing required request in trace {trace.info.trace_id}")
422	            return []
423	        elif not response and judge_requires_outputs:
424	            _logger.warning(f"Missing required response in trace {trace.info.trace_id}")
425	            return []
426	        elif not expectations and judge_requires_expectations:
427	            _logger.warning(f"Missing required expectations in trace {trace.info.trace_id}")
428	            return []
429	
430	        # Find all human assessments for this judge
431	        matching_assessments = []
432	
433	        if trace.info.assessments:
434	            sanitized_judge_name = _sanitize_assessment_name(judge.name)
435	            matching_assessments = [
436	                a
437	                for a in trace.info.assessments
438	                if _sanitize_assessment_name(a.name) == sanitized_judge_name
439	                and a.source.source_type == AssessmentSourceType.HUMAN
440	            ]
441	
442	        if not matching_assessments:
443	            _logger.warning(
444	                f"No human assessment found for judge '{judge.name}' in trace {trace.info.trace_id}"
445	            )
446	            return []

448	        assessments_with_feedback = [a for a in matching_assessments if a.feedback]
449	        if not assessments_with_feedback:
450	            _logger.warning(f"No feedback found in assessments for trace {trace.info.trace_id}")
451	            return []
452	
453	        resolved_assessments = _resolve_assessment_conflicts(assessments_with_feedback)

455	        if len(resolved_assessments) < len(assessments_with_feedback):
456	            discarded = [a for a in assessments_with_feedback if a not in resolved_assessments]

458	                f"[assessment_id='{a.assessment_id}', source_id='{a.source.source_id}', "

465	            )

467	        # Build example kwargs (same for all examples from this trace)

472	            example_inputs.append("trace")

542	    """Simple agreement metric for judge optimization."""
543	    try:
544	        # Extract result from example and prediction
545	        expected = getattr(example, "result", None)
546	        predicted = getattr(pred, "result", None)
547	
548	        if expected is None or predicted is None:
549	            return False

553	        predicted_norm = str(predicted).lower().strip()

563	def append_input_fields_section(instructions: str, judge: "Judge") -> str:
564	    """
565	    Append a section listing the input fields for assessment to the instructions.
566	
567	    DSPy optimizers may modify instructions during optimization. This function
568	    ensures that the input field names are clearly documented at the end of
569	    the instructions, but only if they're not already present.
570	
571	    Args:
572	        instructions: The optimized instructions
573	        judge: The original judge (to get field names)
574	
575	    Returns:
576	        Instructions with input fields section appended, or original instructions
577	        if all input fields are already present
578	    """
579	    input_fields = judge.get_input_fields()
580	    field_names = [f.name for f in input_fields]
581	
582	    if not field_names:
583	        return instructions
584	
585	    # Check if all input fields are already present in mustached format
586	    # Support both {{field}} and {{ field }} formats
587	    def has_mustached_field(name: str) -> bool:
588	        return f"{{{{{name}}}}}" in instructions or f"{{{{ {name} }}}}" in instructions
589	
590	    if all(has_mustached_field(name) for name in field_names):
591	        return instructions
592	
593	    fields_list = ", ".join(f"{{{{ {name} }}}}" for name in field_names)
594	    return f"{instructions}\n\nInputs for assessment: {fields_list}"
595

597	def format_demos_as_examples(demos: list[Any], judge: "Judge") -> str:
598	    """Format demos as few-shot examples to include in judge instructions.
599	
600	    SIMBA optimization adds successful examples to program.demos. This function
601	    converts them to a text format suitable for inclusion in the judge prompt.
602	
603	    Args:
604	        demos: List of dspy.Example objects containing successful judge evaluations
605	        judge: The original judge (to get field names)
606	
607	    Returns:
608	        Formatted text with examples, or empty string if no valid demos
609	    """
610	    if not demos:
611	        return ""
612	
613	    # Get field names from the judge
614	    input_fields = [f.name for f in judge.get_input_fields()]
615	    output_fields = [f.name for f in judge.get_output_fields()]
616	
617	    examples_text = []
618	    for i, demo in enumerate(demos):
619	        example_parts = []
620	
621	        # Access demo fields using dict-style access
622	        # (getattr conflicts with dspy.Example's built-in methods like inputs())
623	        if not hasattr(demo, "items"):
624	            raise MlflowException(
625	                f"Demo at index {i} cannot be converted to dict. "
626	                f"Expected dspy.Example, got {type(demo).__name__}",
627	                error_code=INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
628	            )
629	        demo_dict = dict(demo)
630	
631	        # Format input fields
632	        for field in input_fields:
633	            if field in demo_dict:
634	                value = demo_dict[field]
635	                example_parts.append(f"{field}: {value}")
636	
637	        # Format output fields
638	        for field in output_fields:
639	            if field in demo_dict:
640	                value = demo_dict[field]
641	                example_parts.append(f"{field}: {value}")
642	
643	        if example_parts:
644	            examples_text.append(f"Example {i + 1}:\n" + "\n".join(example_parts))
645	
646	    if examples_text:
647	        return "Here are some examples of good assessments:\n\n" + "\n\n".join(examples_text)
648	    return ""

REFERENCE_MAP = _get_reference_map()


def resolve_missing_references(app, doctree):
    for node in doctree.traverse(condition=pending_xref):
        missing_ref = node.get("reftarget", None)
        if missing_ref is not None and missing_ref in REFERENCE_MAP:
            real_ref = REFERENCE_MAP[missing_ref]
            text_to_render = real_ref.split(".")[-1]
            node["reftarget"] = real_ref
            text_node = next(iter(node.traverse(lambda n: n.tagname == "#text")))
            text_node.parent.replace(text_node, Text(text_to_render, ""))


def env_updated(app: Sphinx, env: BuildEnvironment) -> None:
    items: list[str] = []
    for _domain_name, domain in env.domains.items():
        for _name, display_name, obj_type, _doc_name, _anchor, _priority in domain.get_objects():
            if obj_type in ("function", "method", "class"):
                items.append(display_name)

    repo_root = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], text=True).strip()
    path = Path(repo_root, "docs", "api_reference", "api_inventory.txt")
    if not path.parent.exists():
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    path.write_text("\n".join(sorted(items)) + "\n")


class TestCodeBlockDirective(CodeBlock):
    """

    The actual test extraction is done by the standalone testcode_block.py script.

    option_spec = {**CodeBlock.option_spec, "test": directives.flag}


def setup(app):
    languagesections.setup(app)
    app.add_directive("code-block", TestCodeBlockDirective, override=True)
    app.connect("doctree-read", resolve_missing_references)

5	
6	import { APILink } from "@site/src/components/APILink";
7	
8	# Pickle-Free Model format
9	
10	:::note[Experimental]
11	This feature is experimental and may change in future releases.
12	:::
13	
14	Saving models with Python's `pickle` or `cloudpickle` relies on Python's object serialization mechanism, which can execute arbitrary code during deserialization. MLflow supports safer **pickle-free** saving formats for several model flavors. Prefer these formats when possible.
15	
16	:::warning[Upcoming Default Behavior Change]
17	Pickle-free saving formats will become the **default** in an upcoming MLflow release. **Most users (scikit-learn, LightGBM, LangChain, custom Python) will see no breaking change.** PyTorch users should review the [requirements](#pickle-free-format-for-pytorch-model) — `input_example` will be required and `torch.jit.ScriptModule` is not supported.
18	To avoid getting affected by the change, pin the MLflow version or specify `serialization_format="pickle"` in the model logging code.
19	:::
20	
21	## Pickle-free format for Scikit-learn model
22	
23	When saving a scikit-learn model, set the parameter `serialization_format="skops"` to use the **skops** format for safe deserialization of scikit-learn models. The `skops` format does not rely on Python's pickle and avoids arbitrary code execution when loading.
24	
25	```python
26	import mlflow
27	from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
28	from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
29	
30	X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
31	model = DecisionTreeClassifier().fit(X, y)
32	
33	with mlflow.start_run():
34	    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(
35	        model,
36	        name="model",
37	        serialization_format="skops",
38	    )
39	```
40	
41	For some scikit-learn models that contain custom or third-party types, you need to set `skops_trusted_types` to a list of fully qualified type names so skops can load them. For example, a pipeline with a custom transformer must list that transformer's type as trusted:
42	
43	```python
44	from numpy.random import randint
45	from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin
46	import pandas as pd
47	from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
48	
49	
50	class CustomTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
51	    def fit(self, X, y=None):
52	        return self
53	
54	    def transform(self, X, y=None):
55	        # Perform arbitrary transformation
56	        X["random_int"] = randint(0, 10, X.shape[0])
57	        return X
58	
59	
60	df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6], "c": [7, 8, 9]})
61	
62	pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[("use_custom_transformer", CustomTransformer())])
63	
64	# Custom classes must be marked as trusted for skops
65	with mlflow.start_run():
66	    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(
67	        pipeline,
68	        name="model",
69	        serialization_format="skops",
70	        skops_trusted_types=["__main__.CustomTransformer"],
71	    )
72	```
73	
74	See <APILink fn="mlflow.sklearn.log_model" /> and <APILink fn="mlflow.sklearn.save_model" /> for full parameters.
75	
76	## SHAP explainers remain pickle-based
77	
78	<APILink fn="mlflow.shap.log_explainer" /> and <APILink fn="mlflow.shap.save_explainer" /> use pickle-based serialization for the SHAP explainer state, so the complete artifact is not pickle-free. For a scikit-learn-backed explainer, MLflow also uses cloudpickle for its extracted nested model. Using skops only for that nested model—or automatically trusting classes that skops rejects—would not make the complete SHAP artifact pickle-free or safe to load from an untrusted source.
79	
80	Treat SHAP explainers as pickle-based artifacts and load them only from trusted sources. Setting [`MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false`](#global-configuration-to-force-mlflow-pickle-free-model-loading) prevents them from loading outside Databricks Runtime and Databricks Model Serving. This SHAP-specific behavior does not change models saved directly with `mlflow.sklearn`: standalone sklearn models still use skops by default and can accept explicitly reviewed `skops_trusted_types`.
81	
82	## Pickle-free format for PyTorch model
83	
84	When saving a PyTorch model, saving with `serialization_format="pt2"` uses `torch.export.save` and stores the model as a traced graph instead of pickle serialization format.
85	
86	:::danger[Requirements and Limitations]
87	
88	- `torch` >= 2.4 (`torch` >= 2.10 is required to load the model when `MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false`, see [below](#global-configuration-to-force-mlflow-pickle-free-model-loading))
89	- An **input_example** is required (and only `Tensor` type inputs are supported for the exported model)
90	- Not supported for `torch.jit.ScriptModule` models
91	- Model weights **cannot be transferred between devices** after loading. If the model is saved with weights on GPU device 0, it must also be loaded onto GPU device 0 — not CPU or a different GPU.
92	- To avoid these limitations, use the pickle-based serialization by setting `serialization_format="pickle"`.
93	  :::
94	
95	```python
96	import mlflow
97	import torch
98	from torch import nn
99	from sklearn.datasets import load_diabetes
100	
101	# Load a real dataset and use a sample as the input example
102	X, _ = load_diabetes(return_X_y=True)
103	input_example = torch.tensor(X[:5], dtype=torch.float32).numpy()
104	sequential_model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 3), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(3, 1))
105	with mlflow.start_run():
106	    mlflow.pytorch.log_model(
107	        sequential_model,
108	        name="model",
109	        serialization_format="pt2",
110	        input_example=input_example,
111	    )
112	```
113	
114	See <APILink fn="mlflow.pytorch.log_model" /> and <APILink fn="mlflow.pytorch.save_model" /> for details.
115	
116	## Pickle-free format for LightGBM model
117	
118	For LightGBM models that are scikit-learn model types (e.g., `LGBMClassifier`, `LGBMRegressor`), you can use the **skops** format. This does not apply to `lightgbm.Booster` instances, which use a native format.
119	
120	```python
121	import mlflow
122	from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier
123	from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
124	
125	X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
126	model = LGBMClassifier(objective="multiclass", random_state=42).fit(X, y)
127	
128	with mlflow.start_run():
129	    mlflow.lightgbm.log_model(
130	        model,
131	        name="model",
132	        serialization_format="skops",
133	        skops_trusted_types=[
134	            "collections.OrderedDict",
135	            "lightgbm.basic.Booster",
136	            "lightgbm.sklearn.LGBMClassifier",
137	        ],
138	    )
139	```
140	
141	See <APILink fn="mlflow.lightgbm.log_model" /> and <APILink fn="mlflow.lightgbm.save_model" /> for details.
142	
143	## Pickle-free format for LangChain model
144	
145	LangChain model supports saving as **Models From Code** artifacts, which avoids pickle entirely. For details and examples, see [Models From Code](/ml/model/models-from-code).
146	
147	## Pickle-free format for custom Python model
148	
149	Custom Python model supports saving as **Models From Code** artifacts, which avoids pickle entirely. For details and examples, see [Models From Code](/ml/model/models-from-code).
150	
151	## Global configuration to force MLflow pickle-free model loading
152	
153	You can disallow MLflow model loading with `pickle` or `cloudpickle` globally by setting the environment variable as follows:
154	
155	```bash
156	export MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false
157	```
158	
159	When set to `false`, loading a model that was saved with `pickle` or `cloudpickle` will raise an error unless you use a pickle-free saving option when logging the model. The default is `true` for backward compatibility.
160	
161	:::note[PyTorch `pt2` models]
162	`torch.export.load` internally deserializes parts of a `.pt2` archive with `torch.load(weights_only=False)`. When `MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false`, MLflow therefore verifies before loading that every record in the archive is accepted by torch's restricted `weights_only` unpickler (tensors and primitive containers only), and refuses the model otherwise. This verification requires `torch` >= 2.10 (older versions have known `weights_only` unpickler vulnerabilities); on older versions, loading a `pt2` model with the flag set to `false` raises an error asking you to upgrade `torch` or enable the flag.
163	:::
164	
165	:::note
166	In Databricks Runtime, loading models serialized with `pickle` or `cloudpickle` is always allowed, regardless of the `MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION` environment variable. This is because Databricks uses a managed MLflow artifact store that protects model artifacts from unauthorized modification. By ensuring artifact integrity, the platform mitigates the risk of executing malicious code during `pickle` or `cloudpickle` deserialization.
167	:::
168	
169	## Summary
170	
171	| Flavor              | Pickle-free option             | Notes                                                                                                                            | Impact when becoming default                                                                       |
172	| ------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
173	| Scikit-learn        | `serialization_format="skops"` | Use `skops_trusted_types` when needed.                                                                                           | No impact — transparent upgrade for most models.                                                   |
174	| PyTorch             | `serialization_format="pt2"`   | Requires `input_example`, torch >= 2.4 (>= 2.10 to load with `MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false`); not for ScriptModule. | **Breaking change** — `input_example` will be required; `torch.jit.ScriptModule` is not supported. |
175	| DSPy                | `use_dspy_model_save=True`     | Requires dspy > 3.1.0.                                                                                                           | Requires upgrading to dspy > 3.1.0.                                                                |
176	| LightGBM            | `serialization_format="skops"` | Only for lightGBM models of sklearn type.                                                                                        | No impact — transparent upgrade for sklearn-type LightGBM models.                                  |
177	| LangChain           | Models From Code               | Pickle saving emits warnings.                                                                                                    | No impact.                                                                                         |
178	| Custom Python model | Models From Code               | Pickle saving emits warnings.                                                                                                    | No impact.                                                                                         |

390	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "Span":

392	        try:

394	            request_id = data.get("attributes", {}).get(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID)
395	            if not request_id:
396	                raise MlflowException(
397	                    f"The {SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID} attribute is empty or missing.",
398	                    INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
399	                )
400	
401	            if Span._is_span_v2_schema(data):
402	                return cls.from_dict_v2(data)
403	
404	            if _is_base64_encoded(data["trace_id"]):
405	                otel_trace_id = _decode_id_from_byte(data["trace_id"])
406	                span_id = _decode_id_from_byte(data["span_id"])
407	                # Parent ID always exists in proto (empty string) even if the span is a root span.
408	                parent_id = (
409	                    _decode_id_from_byte(data["parent_span_id"]) if data["parent_span_id"] else None
410	                )
411	            else:
412	                # In 3.5.0, Span.to_dict keeps trace_id and span_id as the object's properties
413	                # format, so we need special handling for it.
414	                otel_trace_id = decode_id(
415	                    parse_trace_id_v4(data["trace_id"])[1].removeprefix(TRACE_REQUEST_ID_PREFIX)
416	                )
417	                span_id = decode_id(data["span_id"])
418	                parent_id = decode_id(data["parent_span_id"]) if data["parent_span_id"] else None
419	
420	            status_code_str = data["status"]["code"]
421	            try:
422	                status_code = SpanStatusCode.from_otel_proto_status_code_name(status_code_str)
423	            except MlflowException:
424	                # In 3.5.0 Span.to_dict keeps status code as the SpanStatusCode enum value
425	                # Fall back to value format (e.g., "OK", "ERROR")
426	                status_code = SpanStatusCode(status_code_str)
427	            status = SpanStatus(
428	                status_code=status_code,
429	                description=data["status"].get("message", ""),
430	            )
431	
432	            end_time_ns = data.get("end_time_unix_nano")
433	            end_time_ns = int(end_time_ns) if end_time_ns else None
434	
435	            otel_span = OTelReadableSpan(
436	                name=data["name"],
437	                context=build_otel_context(otel_trace_id, span_id),
438	                parent=build_otel_context(otel_trace_id, parent_id) if parent_id else None,
439	                start_time=int(data["start_time_unix_nano"]),
440	                end_time=end_time_ns,
441	                attributes=data["attributes"],
442	                status=status.to_otel_status(),
443	                # Setting an empty resource explicitly. Otherwise OTel create a new Resource by
444	                # Resource.create(), which introduces a significant overhead in some environments.
445	                # https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/15625
446	                resource=_OTelResource.get_empty(),
447	                events=[
448	                    OTelEvent(
449	                        name=event["name"],
450	                        timestamp=int(event["time_unix_nano"]),
451	                        attributes=event.get("attributes", {}),
452	                    )
453	                    for event in data.get("events", [])
454	                ],
455	            )

458	            # Deserialize links if present

460	                span._links = [Link.from_dict(link_dict) for link_dict in links_data]

462	            return span

464	            raise MlflowException(
465	                "Failed to create a Span object from the given dictionary",
466	                INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,

507	    @classmethod
508	    def from_otel_proto(
509	        cls,
510	        otel_proto_span: OTelProtoSpan,
511	        location_id: str | None = None,
512	        *,
513	        preserve_request_id: bool = False,
514	        resource: OTelProtoResource | None = None,
515	    ) -> "Span":
516	        """
517	        Create a Span from an OpenTelemetry protobuf span.
518	
519	        This is an internal method used for receiving spans via OTel protocol. By default,
520	        MLflow derives the canonical ``mlflow.traceRequestId`` from the OTLP trace ID so server
521	        ingest does not trust a client-sent request ID. Set ``preserve_request_id=True`` only for
522	        trusted internal round-trip flows, such as archived trace payload deserialization, where
523	        the stored MLflow request ID must be preserved exactly if present.
524	        """
525	        # Validate required fields - empty bytes indicate missing trace_id or span_id
526	        if not otel_proto_span.trace_id:
527	            raise ValueError("trace_id is required but was empty")
528	        if not otel_proto_span.span_id:
529	            raise ValueError("span_id is required but was empty")
530	
531	        trace_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.trace_id)
532	        span_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.span_id)
533	        parent_id = None
534	        if otel_proto_span.parent_span_id:
535	            parent_id = _otel_proto_bytes_to_id(otel_proto_span.parent_span_id)
536	
537	        # Convert OTel proto status code directly to OTel SDK status
538	        if otel_proto_span.status.code == OTelProtoStatus.STATUS_CODE_OK:
539	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.OK
540	        elif otel_proto_span.status.code == OTelProtoStatus.STATUS_CODE_ERROR:
541	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.ERROR
542	        else:
543	            status_code = OTelStatusCode.UNSET
544	
545	        serialized_attributes = {
546	            attr.key: dump_span_attribute_value(_decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value))
547	            for attr in otel_proto_span.attributes
548	        }
549	        mlflow_trace_id = (
550	            generate_trace_id_v4_from_otel_trace_id(trace_id, location_id)
551	            if location_id
552	            else generate_mlflow_trace_id_from_otel_trace_id(trace_id)
553	        )
554	        serialized_request_id = dump_span_attribute_value(mlflow_trace_id)
555	        if preserve_request_id:
556	            serialized_request_id = serialized_attributes.get(
557	                SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID, serialized_request_id
558	            )
559	        request_id = json.loads(serialized_request_id)
560	
561	        # Convert proto Resource to OTel SDK Resource if provided.
562	        # We avoid _OTelResource.create() which has significant overhead from
563	        # environment variable reads (see https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/15625).
564	        if resource is not None and resource.attributes:
565	            resource_attrs = {
566	                attr.key: _decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value) for attr in resource.attributes
567	            }
568	            otel_resource = _OTelResource(resource_attrs)
569	        else:
570	            otel_resource = _OTelResource.get_empty()
571	
572	        links = [Link.from_otel_proto(proto_link) for proto_link in otel_proto_span.links]
573	        for link in links:
574	            link.trace_id = _normalize_link_trace_id(link.trace_id, request_id)
575	
576	        otel_span = OTelReadableSpan(
577	            name=otel_proto_span.name,
578	            context=build_otel_context(trace_id, span_id),
579	            parent=build_otel_context(trace_id, parent_id) if parent_id else None,
580	            start_time=otel_proto_span.start_time_unix_nano,
581	            end_time=otel_proto_span.end_time_unix_nano,
582	            # we need to dump the attribute value to be consistent with span.set_attribute behavior
583	            attributes={
584	                **serialized_attributes,
585	                SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID: serialized_request_id,
586	            },
587	            status=OTelStatus(status_code, otel_proto_span.status.message or None),
588	            events=[
589	                OTelEvent(
590	                    name=event.name,
591	                    timestamp=event.time_unix_nano,
592	                    attributes={
593	                        attr.key: _decode_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value)
594	                        for attr in event.attributes
595	                    },
596	                )
597	                for event in otel_proto_span.events
598	            ],
599	            resource=otel_resource,
600	        )
601	
602	        span = cls(otel_span)
603	        span._links = links
604	        return span
605	
606	    def to_otel_proto(self) -> OTelProtoSpan:
607	        """
608	        Convert to OpenTelemetry protobuf span format for OTLP export.
609	        This is an internal method used by the REST store for logging spans.
610	
611	        Returns:
612	            An OpenTelemetry protobuf Span message.
613	        """
614	        otel_span = OTelProtoSpan()
615	        otel_span.trace_id = bytes.fromhex(self._trace_id)
616	        otel_span.span_id = bytes.fromhex(self.span_id)
617	
618	        otel_span.name = self.name
619	        otel_span.start_time_unix_nano = self.start_time_ns
620	        if self.end_time_ns:
621	            otel_span.end_time_unix_nano = self.end_time_ns
622	
623	        if self.parent_id:
624	            otel_span.parent_span_id = bytes.fromhex(self.parent_id)
625	
626	        otel_span.status.CopyFrom(self.status.to_otel_proto_status())
627	
628	        for key, value in self.attributes.items():
629	            attr = otel_span.attributes.add()
630	            attr.key = key
631	            _set_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value, value)
632	
633	        for event in self.events:
634	            otel_event = event.to_otel_proto()
635	            otel_span.events.append(otel_event)
636	
637	        # Convert links to OTLP proto format
638	        for link in self.links:
639	            proto_link = otel_span.links.add()
640	            # Convert MLflow trace ID (tr-xxx or trace:/loc/xxx) back to OTel bytes
641	            link_trace_id_hex = parse_trace_id_v4(link.trace_id)[1].removeprefix(
642	                TRACE_REQUEST_ID_PREFIX
643	            )
644	            proto_link.trace_id = decode_id(link_trace_id_hex).to_bytes(16, "big")
645	            proto_link.span_id = decode_id(link.span_id).to_bytes(8, "big")
646	
647	            # Add link attributes
648	            if link.attributes:
649	                for key, value in link.attributes.items():
650	                    attr = proto_link.attributes.add()
651	                    attr.key = key
652	                    _set_otel_proto_anyvalue(attr.value, value)
653	
654	        return otel_span
655

685	class LiveSpan(Span):
686	    """
687	    A "live" version of the :py:class:`Span <mlflow.entities.Span>` class.
688	
689	    The live spans are those being created and updated during the application runtime.
690	    When users start a new span using the tracing APIs within their code, this live span
691	    object is returned to get and set the span attributes, status, events, and etc.
692	    """
693	
694	    def __init__(
695	        self,
696	        otel_span: OTelSpan,
697	        trace_id: str,
698	        span_type: str = SpanType.UNKNOWN,
699	    ):
700	        """
701	        The `otel_span` argument takes an instance of OpenTelemetry Span class, which is
702	        indeed a subclass of ReadableSpan. Thanks to this, the getter methods of the Span
703	        class can be reused without any modification.
704	
705	        Note that the constructor doesn't call the super().__init__ method, because the Span
706	        initialization logic is a bit different from the immutable span.
707	        """
708	        if not isinstance(otel_span, OTelReadableSpan):
709	            raise MlflowException(
710	                "The `otel_span` argument for the LiveSpan class must be an instance of "
711	                f"trace.Span, but got {type(otel_span)}.",
712	                INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE,
713	            )
714	
715	        self._span = otel_span
716	        self._attachments: dict[str, Attachment] = {}
717	        self._attributes = _SpanAttributesRegistry(otel_span)
718	        self._attributes.set(SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID, trace_id)
719	        self._attributes.set(SpanAttributeKey.SPAN_TYPE, span_type)
720	        otel_links = getattr(otel_span, "links", ())
721	        self._links: list["Link"] = [
722	            _link_from_otel_link(otel_link, trace_id) for otel_link in otel_links
723	        ]
724	        # Track the original span name for deduplication purposes during span logging.
725	        # Why: When traces contain multiple spans with identical names (e.g., multiple "LLM"
726	        # or "query" spans), it's difficult for users to distinguish between them in the UI
727	        # and logs. As spans are logged, we incrementally add numeric suffixes (_1, _2, etc.) to
728	        # make each span uniquely identifiable within its trace
729	        self._original_name = otel_span.name
730	
731	    def set_span_type(self, span_type: str):
732	        """Set the type of the span."""
733	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.SPAN_TYPE, span_type)
734	
735	    def set_description(self, description: str):
736	        """Set the description of the span."""
737	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.DESCRIPTION, description)

739	    def set_log_level(self, level: SpanLogLevel | str):
740	        """
741	        Set the severity level of the span.
742	
743	        Args:
744	            level: A :py:class:`SpanLogLevel <mlflow.entities.SpanLogLevel>` or
745	                its name (e.g. ``"INFO"``).
746	        """

748	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.LOG_LEVEL, int(normalized))

750	    def _is_recording(self) -> bool:
751	        return self._span.is_recording()

753	    def set_inputs(self, inputs: Any):
754	        """Set the input values to the span."""
755	        extract_base64 = self._should_extract_base64()
756	        inputs = self._extract_attachments(inputs, extract_base64)
757	        self.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.INPUTS, inputs)
758	        # Second pass on the serialized form handles framework objects
759	        # (e.g., Pydantic models, LangChain BaseMessage) that only become
760	        # plain dicts after JSON serialization by set_attribute.
761	        if extract_base64:
762	            self._extract_attachments_from_serialized(SpanAttributeKey.INPUTS)

764	    def set_outputs(self, outputs: Any):
765	        """Set the output values to the span."""

767	        outputs = self._extract_attachments(outputs, extract_base64)

772	    def _extract_attachments_from_serialized(self, attr_key: str):
773	        """Re-extract attachments from the serialized attribute value.
774	
775	        Handles cases where the first extraction pass couldn't recurse into
776	        framework-specific objects (e.g., LangChain BaseMessage) that only
777	        become plain dicts after JSON serialization.
778	        """
779	        serialized = self._attributes.get(attr_key)
780	        if serialized is None:
781	            return
782	        attachments_before = len(self._attachments)
783	        extracted = self._extract_attachments(serialized, extract_base64=True)
784	        if len(self._attachments) > attachments_before:
785	            self.set_attribute(attr_key, extracted)
786	
787	    def _extract_attachments(self, value: Any, extract_base64: bool) -> Any:
788	        if isinstance(value, Attachment):
789	            return self._store_attachment(value)
790	        if extract_base64:
791	            if isinstance(value, str):
792	                converted = self._try_convert_data_uri(value)
793	                if converted is not None:
794	                    return converted
795	            if isinstance(value, dict):
796	                converted = self._try_convert_structured_content(value)
797	                if converted is not None:
798	                    # Recurse into the converted dict to catch remaining patterns
799	                    # in sibling keys (e.g. a data URI in another field)
800	                    if isinstance(converted, dict):
801	                        return {
802	                            k: self._extract_attachments(v, extract_base64)
803	                            for k, v in converted.items()
804	                        }
805	                    return converted
806	        if isinstance(value, dict):
807	            return {k: self._extract_attachments(v, extract_base64) for k, v in value.items()}
808	        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
809	            return [self._extract_attachments(item, extract_base64) for item in value]
810	        return value
811	
812	    def _store_attachment(self, attachment: Attachment) -> str:
813	        from mlflow.environment_variables import MLFLOW_TRACE_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE
814	
815	        if not self._is_recording():
816	            _logger.debug("Skipping attachment storage because the span is no longer recording.")
817	            return attachment.ref(self.trace_id)
818	
819	        max_size = MLFLOW_TRACE_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE.get()
820	        if max_size is not None and max_size > 0 and len(attachment.content_bytes) > max_size:
821	            size_bytes = len(attachment.content_bytes)
822	            msg = (
823	                f"Attachment too large ({size_bytes} bytes > {max_size} bytes limit). "
824	                f"Content discarded."
825	            )
826	            _logger.warning(msg)
827	            self.record_exception(msg)
828	            return f"[Attachment too large: {size_bytes} bytes exceeds {max_size} bytes limit]"
829	        ref = attachment.ref(self.trace_id)
830	        self._attachments[attachment.id] = attachment
831	        return ref
832	
833	    @staticmethod
834	    def _should_extract_base64() -> bool:
835	        from mlflow.environment_variables import MLFLOW_TRACE_EXTRACT_ATTACHMENTS
836	
837	        return MLFLOW_TRACE_EXTRACT_ATTACHMENTS.get()

839	    def _try_convert_data_uri(self, value: str) -> str | None:
840	        if not value.startswith("data:") or ";base64," not in value:
841	            return None
842	        header, _, b64data = value.partition(";base64,")
843	        mime = header[len("data:") :]
844	        if not mime:
845	            return None
846	        try:
847	            content_bytes = base64.b64decode(b64data, validate=True)
848	        except Exception:
849	            return None
850	        return self._store_attachment(Attachment(content_type=mime, content_bytes=content_bytes))
851	
852	    def _try_convert_structured_content(self, value: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | str | None:
853	        # TODO: If this grows unwieldy, consider either (a) splitting into per-provider
854	        # helpers (parse_openai_audio, parse_anthropic_image, etc.) or (b) moving
855	        # extraction into individual autolog integrations as post-execution hooks.
856	        # See: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/21955#discussion_r2999432747
857	
858	        # OpenAI input_audio content part
859	        if value.get("type") == "input_audio" and isinstance(
860	            audio := value.get("input_audio"), dict
861	        ):
862	            data = audio.get("data")
863	            fmt = audio.get("format", "wav")
864	            if isinstance(data, str) and data:
865	                try:
866	                    content_bytes = base64.b64decode(data, validate=True)
867	                except Exception:
868	                    return None
869	                content_type = "audio/mpeg" if fmt == "mp3" else f"audio/{fmt}"
870	                ref = self._store_attachment(
871	                    Attachment(content_type=content_type, content_bytes=content_bytes)
872	                )
873	                return {
874	                    **value,
875	                    "input_audio": {**audio, "data": ref},
876	                }
877	
878	        # Anthropic image content part
879	        if value.get("type") == "image" and isinstance(source := value.get("source"), dict):
880	            if source.get("type") == "base64":
881	                data = source.get("data")
882	                media_type = source.get("media_type", "image/png")
883	                if isinstance(data, str) and data:
884	                    try:
885	                        content_bytes = base64.b64decode(data, validate=True)
886	                    except Exception:
887	                        return None
888	                    ref = self._store_attachment(
889	                        Attachment(content_type=media_type, content_bytes=content_bytes)

1537	class _SpanAttributesRegistry:
1538	    """
1539	    A utility class to manage the span attributes.
1540	
1541	    In MLflow users can add arbitrary key-value pairs to the span attributes, however,
1542	    OpenTelemetry only allows a limited set of types to be stored in the attribute values.
1543	    Therefore, we serialize all values into JSON string before storing them in the span.
1544	    This class provides simple getter and setter methods to interact with the span attributes
1545	    without worrying about the serde process.
1546	    """
1547	
1548	    def __init__(self, otel_span: OTelSpan):
1549	        self._span = otel_span
1550	
1551	    def get_all(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1552	        return {key: self.get(key) for key in self._span.attributes.keys()}
1553	
1554	    def get(self, key: str):
1555	        if serialized_value := self._span.attributes.get(key):
1556	            try:
1557	                return json.loads(serialized_value)
1558	            except Exception:
1559	                # If failed to deserialize (e.g., string value is directly set to OTel span),
1560	                # return the original value as is.
1561	                return serialized_value
1562	
1563	    def set(self, key: str, value: Any):
1564	        if not isinstance(key, str):
1565	            _logger.warning(f"Attribute key must be a string, but got {type(key)}. Skipping.")
1566	            return
1567	
1568	        # NB: OpenTelemetry attribute can store not only string but also a few primitives like
1569	        #   int, float, bool, and list of them. However, we serialize all into JSON string here
1570	        #   for the simplicity in deserialization process.
1571	        self._span.set_attribute(key, dump_span_attribute_value(value))
1572

1574	class _CachedSpanAttributesRegistry(_SpanAttributesRegistry):
1575	    """
1576	    A cache-enabled version of the SpanAttributesRegistry.
1577	
1578	    The caching helps to avoid the redundant deserialization of the attribute, however, it does
1579	    not handle the value change well. Therefore, this class should only be used for the persisted
1580	    spans that are immutable, and thus implemented as a subclass of _SpanAttributesRegistry.
1581	    """
1582	
1583	    def __init__(self, otel_span: OTelSpan):
1584	        super().__init__(otel_span)
1585	        self._cache: dict[str, Any] = {}
1586	
1587	    def get(self, key: str):
1588	        if key not in self._cache:
1589	            self._cache[key] = super().get(key)
1590	        return self._cache[key]
1591	
1592	    def set(self, key: str, value: Any):
1593	        raise MlflowException(
1594	            "The attributes of the immutable span must not be updated.", INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
1595	        )

def _test_model(datetime=datetime.now()):
    class TestModel:
        @mlflow.trace()
        def predict(self, x, y):
            z = x + y
            z = self.add_one(z)
            return z  # noqa: RET504

        @mlflow.trace(
            span_type=SpanType.LLM,
            name="add_one_with_custom_name",
            attributes={
                "delta": 1,
                "metadata": {"foo": "bar"},
                # Test for non-json-serializable input
                "datetime": datetime,
            },
        )
        def add_one(self, z):
            return z + 1

    return TestModel()

def test_trace_to_from_dict_and_json():
    model = _test_model()
    model.predict(2, 5)

    trace = mlflow.get_trace(mlflow.get_last_active_trace_id())

    spans = trace.search_spans(span_type=SpanType.LLM)
    assert len(spans) == 1

    spans = trace.search_spans(name="predict")
    assert len(spans) == 1

    trace_dict = trace.to_dict()
    trace_from_dict = Trace.from_dict(trace_dict)
    trace_json = trace.to_json()
    trace_from_json = Trace.from_json(trace_json)
    for loaded_trace in [trace_from_dict, trace_from_json]:
        assert trace.info == loaded_trace.info
        assert trace.data.request == loaded_trace.data.request
        assert trace.data.response == loaded_trace.data.response
        assert len(trace.data.spans) == len(loaded_trace.data.spans)
        for i in range(len(trace.data.spans)):
            for attr in [
                "name",
                "request_id",
                "span_id",
                "start_time_ns",
                "end_time_ns",
                "parent_id",
                "status",
                "inputs",
                "outputs",
                "_trace_id",
                "attributes",
                "events",
            ]:
                assert getattr(trace.data.spans[i], attr) == getattr(
                    loaded_trace.data.spans[i], attr
                )

6	# Setting Log Levels on Spans
7	
8	Span log levels classify each span by severity, modeled on Python's standard `logging` module. They let you scan a busy trace at a glance: at the default threshold the trace renders unchanged, but bumping the **Minimum log level** filter in the UI hides noise (chain plumbing, output parsing) so you see only the user-visible operations, such as requests, responses, tool calls.
9	
10	The five levels share names with Python's `logging` module:
11	
12	| Level      | Typical use                                      |
13	| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
14	| `DEBUG`    | Internal/glue work — chain steps, parsers, etc.  |
15	| `INFO`     | User-visible operations — LLM calls, tool calls. |
16	| `WARNING`  | Recoverable issues you'd want to see in prod.    |
17	| `ERROR`    | Failures.                                        |
18	| `CRITICAL` | Hard stops worth paging on.                      |
19	
20	## Setting the level on a span
21	
22	You can pass a level when you create the span. The kwarg accepts the enum value or its name.

73	## Default Log Level
74	
75	Every span, whether created manually or by an autolog integration (`mlflow.openai.autolog()`, `mlflow.langchain.autolog()`, etc.), is assigned a default level based on its span type. This ensures the verbosity filter works out of the box without you annotating anything. The default is applied in the span constructor, and can be overridden by passing an explicit `log_level` keyword argument.
76	
77	| Span type                                                                                                           | Default |
78	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
79	| `LLM`, `CHAT_MODEL`, `TOOL`, `RETRIEVER`, `AGENT`, `EMBEDDING`                                                      | `INFO`  |
80	| Everything else (`CHAIN`, `PARSER`, `RERANKER`, `MEMORY`, `WORKFLOW`, `TASK`, `EVALUATOR`, `UNKNOWN`, custom types) | `DEBUG` |
81	
82	So at the default UI threshold (`DEBUG`) you see everything, at `INFO` you see the user-visible operations and lose the chain plumbing, and at `WARNING`+ you only see spans you've explicitly marked above that level.
83	
84	### Spans with an exception event are bumped to `ERROR`
85	
86	When a span records an exception event, MLflow automatically elevates its level to `ERROR` (unless it is already at a higher severity). Exception events may arise from:
87	
88	- An unhandled exception captured by the @mlflow.trace decorator
89	- An explicit call to span.record_exception(...)
90	- A tracer-level error handler
91	
92	This ensures that failures remain visible in the trace explorer, even when the user raises the verbosity filter.
93	
94	## Applying Log Level Filter on UI
95	
96	Open a trace in the MLflow UI and click **Filter** above the timeline tree. The popover has a **Minimum log level** slider (with a "?" tooltip explaining the rules):
97	
98	- **Debug** (default) — show every span.
99	- **Info** — hide `DEBUG` spans (most chain plumbing disappears).
100	- **Warning / Error / Critical** — only spans explicitly marked at or above the threshold.
101	
102	The existing **Show all parent spans** and **Show exceptions** toggles still apply: they override the level filter so you don't lose context for matched children or for spans that recorded an exception.
103	
104	## Backwards compatibility
105	
106	Some spans may not have an `mlflow.spanLogLevel` attribute. This can happen for traces logged before span log levels were introduced, or for spans produced by third-party tracers that do not assign a level. The UI treats these spans as `DEBUG`, so they remain visible at the default threshold. Raising the threshold to `INFO` or higher hides them along with other `DEBUG` spans. To make a specific span visible again, you can explicitly set its level using `set_log_level`.
107	
108	## API References
109	
110	- <APILink fn="mlflow.entities.SpanLogLevel" /> — the level enum.
111	- <APILink fn="mlflow.start_span" /> / <APILink fn="mlflow.start_span_no_context" /> / <APILink fn="mlflow.trace" /> — public APIs that accept the `log_level` kwarg.

569	        with mlflow.start_span("my_span") as span:
570	            x = 1
571	            y = 2
572	            span.set_inputs({"x": x, "y": y})
573	
574	            z = x + y
575	
576	            span.set_outputs(z)
577	            span.set_attribute("key", "value")
578	            # do something

580	    When this context manager is used in the top-level scope, i.e. not within another span context,
581	    the span will be treated as a root span. The root span doesn't have a parent reference and
582	    **the entire trace will be logged when the root span is ended**.
583	
584	
585	    .. tip::
586	
587	        If you want more explicit control over the trace lifecycle, you can use
588	        the `mlflow.start_span_no_context()` API. It provides lower
589	        level to start spans and control the parent-child relationships explicitly.
590	        However, it is generally recommended to use this context manager as long as it satisfies
591	        your requirements, because it requires less boilerplate code and is less error-prone.
592	
593	    .. note::
594	
595	        The context manager doesn't propagate the span context across threads by default. see
596	        `Multi Threading <https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracing/api/manual-instrumentation#multi-threading>`_
597	        for how to propagate the span context across threads.
598	
599	    Args:
600	        name: The name of the span.
601	        span_type: The type of the span. Can be either a string or
602	            a :py:class:`SpanType <mlflow.entities.SpanType>` enum value
603	        attributes: A dictionary of attributes to set on the span.
604	        trace_destination: The destination to log the trace to, such as MLflow Experiment. If
605	            not provided, the destination will be an active MLflow experiment or an destination

608	            ignored with a warning.

610	            :py:class:`SpanLogLevel <mlflow.entities.SpanLogLevel>` or its name
611	            (e.g. ``"INFO"``, ``"DEBUG"``). If not provided, the span level is
612	            resolved from the span type at end time.

614	            only applied when creating a root span. If provided without an explicit
615	            `trace_destination`, the trace will be logged to the run's experiment. If an
616	            active MLflow run is already set via `mlflow.start_run()`, this parameter takes
617	            precedence over the active run.
618	        links: A list of :py:class:`Link <mlflow.entities.Link>` objects to associate with
619	            the span.
620	        description: An optional human-readable description of the span.
621	
622	    Returns:
623	        Yields an :py:class:`mlflow.entities.Span` that represents the created span.
624	    """
625	    # If tracing is disabled via context(enabled=False), return NoOpSpan
626	    config = _USER_TRACE_CONTEXT.get()
627	    if config is not None and config.enabled is False:
628	        yield NoOpSpan()
629	        return
630	
631	    try:
632	        experiment_id = getattr(trace_destination, "experiment_id", None)
633	
634	        otel_span = provider.start_span_in_context(
635	            name,
636	            experiment_id=experiment_id,
637	        )
638	
639	        # If the span was dropped by the sampler (e.g., due to sampling ratio),
640	        # still propagate the OTel context so that child spans inherit the same
641	        # trace ID and are also consistently dropped.
642	        if not otel_span.is_recording():
643	            noop_span = NoOpSpan(otel_span=otel_span)
644	        else:
645	            noop_span = None
646	
647	            # Create a new MLflow span and register it to the in-memory trace manager
648	            request_id = get_otel_attribute(otel_span, SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID)
649	
650	            # SpanProcessor should have already registered the span in the in-memory trace manager
651	            trace_manager = InMemoryTraceManager.get_instance()
652	            mlflow_span = trace_manager.get_span_from_id(
653	                request_id, encode_span_id(otel_span.context.span_id)
654	            )
655	            mlflow_span.set_span_type(span_type)
656	            attributes = dict(attributes) if attributes is not None else {}
657	            mlflow_span.set_attributes(attributes)
658	            if description is not None:
659	                mlflow_span.set_attribute(SpanAttributeKey.DESCRIPTION, description)
660	            if log_level is not None:
661	                mlflow_span.set_log_level(log_level)
662	
663	            if run_id is not None:
664	                if mlflow_span.parent_id is not None:
665	                    _logger.warning(
666	                        "The `run_id` parameter can only be used for root spans, but the span "
667	                        f"`{name}` is not a root span. The specified value `{run_id}` "
668	                        "will be ignored."
669	                    )
670	                else:
671	                    with trace_manager.get_trace(request_id) as trace:
672	                        trace.info.trace_metadata[TraceMetadataKey.SOURCE_RUN] = run_id
673	
674	    except Exception:
675	        _logger.debug(f"Failed to start span {name}.", exc_info=True)
676	        noop_span = NoOpSpan()
677	
678	    if noop_span is None:
679	        for link in links or []:
680	            try:
681	                mlflow_span.add_link(link)
682	            except MlflowException:
683	                _logger.warning("Skipping invalid link: %s", link)
684	
685	    # Yield NoOp spans outside the try/except block so that exceptions thrown
686	    # back into the generator (via contextmanager's throw()) propagate correctly
687	    # instead of being caught by the broad "except Exception" above.
688	    if noop_span is not None:

690	            yield noop_span

693	    try:

697	        try:
698	            mlflow_span.end()
699	        except Exception:
700	            _logger.debug(f"Failed to end span {mlflow_span.span_id}.", exc_info=True)
